💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated on November 16th, 2026 - Version: 1.9.7 (Honor Arena).
  • Industry observers note that do you want to know what the best gear is in Capybara Go?
  • You want your Capybara hero to be strong, so having a good build is half of that particular battle already.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated on November 16th, 2026 - Version: 1.9.7 (Honor Arena).

Industry observers note that do you want to know what the best gear is in Capybara Go? Then let me tell you all about that because today we've got a complete Capybara Go tier list where we not only discuss weapons and armor, but also everything else you can equip.

You want your Capybara hero to be strong, so having a good build is half of that particular battle already. The rest is, of course, having the right daily encounters and a little bit of luck. But we're not talking about luck today, we're talking about factual stuff that you can have a say in. About this Capybara Go tier list I have compared all the gear you can at the moment get in Capybara Go, as well as all the pets and skills and ranked them into a Capybara Go tier list. The best choices are right at the very top, while the ones that might not be worth your investment sit in the lower tiers.

I made this list based on my experience and on my gameplay style, so a few things might differ for you. However, as a general rule of thumb, the top 2 tiers are universally the best, regardless of where I ranked a specific item.

Sources indicate that as you can see, there are quite a few rarities of pets sitting atop our Capybara Go tier list of pets. That's mainly because it is extremely difficult to get an Immortal pet such as Elsa (who is also a beast), so a good alternative is going for Ice Wind Fox and Little Elle.

These two are staples in most builds, and you can easily pick one of the others whenever you get them. But given these two are Legendary rarity, chances are you'll get them a lot easier.

Sources indicate that as for the others, I personally used Snowy and Chomper as much as I could at the beginning, until I managed to summon something better. They are okay since they can grant some useful effects, and for some Epic pets, they perform really well.

In a recent development, upgrading all of your pets is something you should always do since they give you bonus passives. You don't have to use them for the active skills, just for the Upgrade Effects they provide. Upgrade them all to at least +5 (for the Hero ATK).

I need to make it very clear that skills are entirely dependent on the play style, the build you want to go for, and the gear. The skills you pick should always have good synergy with your gear, which is why I mention it in the Gear tier list when discussing situational weapons.

Now there are a lot of skills, and sometimes you will not be able to pick all the best ones. With this Capybara Go skills tier list, I hope I'll give you a clearer understanding of where each skill lands, generally speaking.

It has been revealed that in some situations, some skills might be better and some might be worse. Take this tier list as a baseline, but always adjust it to your build.

S tier - these are generally good. You can't go wrong if you pick one of these for your build, especially since they are versatile and have the Global ATK +25% buff.

Industry observers note that A tier - these are situational items. Depending on your play style, they could be even S-tier or S+ tier, but it also depends on the rest of your gear and the skills you go for.

In a recent development, B tier - Decent, but you can do better. Use this gear until you get something else. Non-S gear tier list Tier Gear name S Warrior's Sword, Warrior's Blade, Frostbite Spear, Tunic A Nomad Bow, Hawkeye Bow, Silverscale Plate, Guardian's Ring, Frostwind Horn, Icy Bubble B Nomad Staff, Forest Staff, Hard Armor, Magic Ring, Vitality Stone C Giant's Hammer, Mystic Staff, Eagle Ring D Nomad Sword.

This gear is also pretty good. Considering how many copies it takes to get the S-Gear, you might sometimes be better off with these. I personally think the Frostwind Horn can be a great item, especially if you go for a full frost setup.

As for the rest, the Warrior's Blade goes really well with CRIT Mastery, so if you do get them both, you will have a really solid baseline for what the rest of your skills should be.

And that's our Capybara Go tier list with all the pets, skills and gear in the game at the moment. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the Acura Integra Type S is the swankier cousin of the boy-racer Honda Civic Type R.
  • An expertly tuned chassis gives the Integra Type S high-spirited handling, and it rides comfortably enough for long trips.
  • Expert Tip: Its premium badge and $ 56,000 price tag put the Integra Type S into contention with some European rivals that offer richer accommodations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Acura Integra Type S is the swankier cousin of the boy-racer Honda Civic Type R. The two share their mechanical underpinnings and hatchback body style, but the Acura is dressed in a more respectable-looking outfit. A lusty 320-hp turbocharged inline-four is under the hood and mates exclusively to a six-speed manual transmission. The combination loves to spin its front tires excitedly, and it's a riot to drive.

An expertly tuned chassis gives the Integra Type S high-spirited handling, and it rides comfortably enough for long trips. The engineers responsible for this gem had driving enthusiasts in mind when this Acura was planned. The cabin is slightly upscale from the Civic Type-R as well, although not as much as you’d think given the six grand price delta between the two.

Expert Tip: Its premium badge and $ 56,000 price tag put the Integra Type S into contention with some European rivals that offer richer accommodations.

Compare the 2027 Acura Integra Type S with the top vehicles in this segment with our fresh compare tool.

Acura has added a limited-production Heritage Edition to the lineup for 2027. Only 700 will be offered in the U.S., all painted Blazing Phoenix Yellow and wearing special copper-colored aluminum wheels. The Heritage Edition is also emblazoned with black exterior badging and features a titanium shift knob.

The standard Integra Type S gets a few changes for the 2027 model year, too, including upcoming gloss black wheels, yellow brake calipers, dark gray interior trim, and gloss black climate control knobs. Several features have been added as standard, such as memory settings for the driver’s seat and an exterior mirror tilt-down feature that can be set to automatically dip the mirrors when you shift into reverse.

Industry observers note that if this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying new.

Sources indicate that A 320-hp turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-four with 310 pound-feet of torque is the sole engine for the Integra Type S. Like the Civic Type R, the Integra Type S routes the power exclusively through a six-speed manual transmission and front-wheel drive with a limited-slip differential. Shifter action is wonderfully light and precise—this is one of the best manual shifters in the business—and clutch take-up is smooth and intuitive. With all 310 pound-feet of torque available at 2600 rpm, you could skip a shift or two without worry, but it'd be a shame to miss out on all the fun.

Objectively, roadholding and braking match the Civic Type R, with the Integra Type S pulling 1.02 g's on the skid pad and stopping from 70 mph in just 153 feet. Subjectively, the Civic feels ever so slightly more vivacious from behind the wheel. The Integra Type S knows how to chill in less demanding situations, slipping into an almost-calm cruising mode. All Type S models come with 19-inch wheels wearing summer tires, Brembo brakes, and an exhaust system with three center-mounted exhaust pipes.

Car and Driver calculates your car's value in three free and easy steps - using the same Black Book® data dealers use to appraise vehicles.

In Comparison: The Integra Type S's brisk 60-mph sprint time is nearly two seconds quicker than the 7.0-second time we posted with the standard six-speed Integra and just 0.2 seconds behind the last Civic Type R we tested.

The EPA estimates that the Integra Type S will deliver 21 mpg city, 28 mpg highway, and 24 mpg combined. It's also worth noting the Type S returned an impressive 31 mpg on our 75-mph highway fuel-economy test, three miles per gallon better than its EPA rating. For more information about the Integra Type S's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

In Comparison: The Audi S3 is slightly more efficient, earning EPA estimates of 23 mpg city and 31 mpg highway, as is the BMW M235 Gran Coupe with estimates of 24 mpg city and 33 mpg highway.

Industry observers note that first Row: Acura plays the long game with the Type S's interior, favoring conservative design and quality materials over outright flash. There are plenty of parts shared with the Honda Civic under the skin, but Acura pulls styling elements from its SUVs to foster the familial vibe. Distinctive features include mildly bolstered sport seats upholstered with perforated, faux-suede fabric, “Type S” embossed headrests, and subtle touches including a Type S shift knob, boot, and steering wheel emblem.

Second Row: A pair of individual rear bucket seats and a small center console armrest replace the standard Integra's rear bench. There's room for two in back, but the lack of features such as rear air vents and seat heaters is a notable omission in a supposedly premium car.

Sources indicate that cargo Capacity: Thanks to its Civic roots, the Integra Type S offers the same 24 cubic feet of cargo room accessed via a large hatchback. We fit five carry-on suitcases in the trunk and managed to squeeze in a total of 18 with the rear seats folded.

The Type S gets the same 10.2-inch digital gauge cluster as the rest of the Integra lineup; a 9.0-inch infotainment touchscreen is standard. A wireless smartphone charging pad, a head-up display, and a pair of USB ports are also included. All versions come with a top-tier 16-speaker, 530-watt ELS Studio 3D premium audio system.

A host of driver-assistance features are included as standard in the Integra Type S, including automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection, lane-keeping assist, and adaptive cruise control.

For information about the Integra Type S's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

Acura offers a longer powertrain warranty than most of its competitors, with powertrain coverage stretching up to six years or 70,000 miles. Complimentary scheduled maintenance is also included, unlike the Audi S3 or the Mercedes-Benz CLA-Class.

Tesla on Autopilot/FSD was going 74 mph before fiery crash that killed 3

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1159 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Tesla Model Y left a parkway in El Dorado Hills, California, hit a tree and burst into flames in September, killing three of the four people inside.
  • Sources indicate that the crash was widely covered in the Sacramento area as a fiery single-car wreck.
  • It has been revealed that late on Saturday, September 12, 2026, a 2024 Tesla Model Y with four people inside was heading west on Serrano Parkway, between Terracina Drive and Silva Valley Parkway.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Tesla Model Y left a parkway in El Dorado Hills, California, hit a tree and burst into flames in September, killing three of the four people inside. Tesla’s own report to federal regulators says Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” was engaged, with the car doing 74 mph.

Sources indicate that the crash was widely covered in the Sacramento area as a fiery single-car wreck. None of that coverage mentioned a driver-assist system. It’s the latest case in our ongoing investigation into fatal crashes hidden in Tesla’s NHTSA data.

It has been revealed that late on Saturday, September 12, 2026, a 2024 Tesla Model Y with four people inside was heading west on Serrano Parkway, between Terracina Drive and Silva Valley Parkway. That’s a residential part of the Serrano community in El Dorado Hills, east of Sacramento.

According to the CHP’s Placerville office, the Model Y left the road “for unknown reasons,” hit a tree on the north side of the parkway, and caught fire. Officers got the call around 10:38 p.m. By the time they arrived, the car was fully engulfed in flames.

Charles Anthony Cameron, 30, of Sacramento, was thrown from the car and died at the scene. Alejandra Mendoza, 28, of Sacramento, and Kailauna Viola Mills, 28, of Roseville, were found dead inside once firefighters put out the fire. One of the two women was driving; CHP hasn’t publicly remarked which.

Mills lived in Arizona and was visiting family. Her uncle told CBS Sacramento she worked in the medical field and was supposed to get married next April.

A fourth person, a 28-year-old Sacramento woman, survived with major injuries.

CHP claims the cause is still under investigation. Speed, impairment, and how the car left the road haven’t been released. And nobody has said a word about Autopilot.

Industry observers note that under NHTSA’s Standing General Order, automakers have to report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone is killed or hurt. Tesla filed a report on this one.

According to recent reports, it lists a 2024 Model Y, a consumer vehicle, and marks the “Engagement Status” as “Verified Engaged.” That’s Tesla confirming through its own telematics that Autopilot or FSD was on. It logs a pre-crash speed of 74 mph, a fatality, and the California Highway Patrol as the investigating agency.

Then it redacts the narrative, the software version, and whether the road was inside the system’s operating domain, all as “confidential business information,” the same treatment Tesla gives 99.9% of its reports.

The rest of the report is strangely thin. Tesla lists the roadway type as “Unknown” and what the car hit as “Unknown,” even though police remarked it was a tree. It checks only one source for how it learned of the crash: the media. So Tesla found out about a triple-fatal crash in one of its cars from the news, then went into its own data and confirmed its driver-assist was on.

Recent findings suggest that how we matched it: Tesla logged the incident time as 05:36 UTC, which is 10:36 p.m. Pacific on September 12, within two minutes of the 10:38 p.m. call CHP responded to. The city, the 2024 Model Y, the month, and the fatal outcome all line up. It’s the only fatal Tesla driver-assist report from El Dorado Hills in the data. It’s the same crash.

Two of the three victims were found inside the car after the fire was out. The survivor got out of, or was pulled from, the wreckage, depending on the report.

CHP hasn’t said whether the doors played any role, and we’re not suggesting they did. But it’s a fair question to ask about any Tesla crash with a fire, now that NHTSA is writing latest rules for emergency door releases after years of complaints about people getting trapped. We’ve asked.

This is the second triple-fatal crash in Tesla’s latest NHTSA filings where its driver-assist was verified engaged and the public never heard about it. The other one was on I-75 in Naples. Add Vineland and July’s four fatal crashes, and the pattern is hard to miss.

What stands out in this one is how little effort went into the report. Tesla knows the speed, knows the system was on, and has telematics. But it couldn’t fill in what the car hit, and it learned about three deaths in one of its cars from the news. Then it redacted the one field, the narrative, that would tell us what the car did.

Tesla wants regulators and customers to trust FSD with no one watching. That trust has to be earned with data. A manufacturer that seals the account of what its car did at 74 mph in a neighborhood, in a crash that killed three people, isn’t earning it.

After 15 years, The Sims' best spin-off finally gets its due follow-up in The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events.
  • Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.
  • In a recent development, there’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

In a recent development, there’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a upcoming world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

It has been revealed that ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Industry observers note that speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a latest Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Swordsmanship is the latest 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of fresh careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

In a recent development, of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

Recent findings suggest that in November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing fresh free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

According to recent reports, while you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free upgrade, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

Latest Update: 10 Games That Have Creative Punishments for Cheating

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that it’ll come as no surprise to any gamer that pretty much every game has a way to cheat, whether it's approved by the developers or otherwise.
  • While a lot of the punishments for cheating in more recent years are typical things like warnings or outright bans, there are some that take a more creative approach.
  • This list consists of many games from all sorts of genres and ages, but they all have some interesting and hilarious punishments for what they perceive as cheating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it’ll come as no surprise to any gamer that pretty much every game has a way to cheat, whether it's approved by the developers or otherwise. Over the years there have been some pretty creative and hilarious ways that developers have dealt with cheaters in all kinds of games from FPS games to the cozy ones.

While a lot of the punishments for cheating in more recent years are typical things like warnings or outright bans, there are some that take a more creative approach. Whether it’s a fun way to kill the player or an incredibly punishing turn of events for dark deeds, it’s always funny to see that happen.

This list consists of many games from all sorts of genres and ages, but they all have some interesting and hilarious punishments for what they perceive as cheating. It may not always be altering game files and could just be something players are able to abuse in game.

Sources indicate that way back in 1996 Crusader: No Regret came out following in the footsteps of its predecessor Crusader: No Remorse. The isometric gameplay combined with some great weapons and destructive environments made a very engaging combination.

The only problem was if you played the previous game and attempted to use any cheats from the last game Crusader: No Regret would have something to say about it. Players would be greeted with a message and teleported into a room with eight copies of the final boss.

In a recent development, heretic was created using the DOOM engine, but things were a bit mixed up and instead of the traditional DOOM world this one was steeped in fantasy elements. Everything revolved around the fantasy element as players could use magical weapons like the Elven Wand, and Phoenix Rod.

In a recent development, unfortunately for players who were well educated in the ways of DOOM, the developers had a surprise for anyone hoping to use DOOM cheats. #5059. Even occasional marijuana use linked to 40% higher odds of stroke

Even occasional marijuana use linked to 40% higher odds of stroke

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1370 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • New preliminary research involving more than 440,000 American adults has uncovered a concerning association between cannabis use and cardiovascular disease, particularly stroke.
  • The research, presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026, found that the association was not limited to people who frequently used cannabis.
  • Scientific Sessions 2026 took place November 6 through 9 in Chicago, bringing together cardiovascular researchers and healthcare professionals from around the world to share scientific discoveries, clinical advances, and emerging evidence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

New preliminary research involving more than 440,000 American adults has uncovered a concerning association between cannabis use and cardiovascular disease, particularly stroke. The findings suggest that even occasional marijuana use may be linked to higher odds of cardiovascular problems, raising new questions about the health effects of a substance that is becoming increasingly common across the United States.

The research, presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026, found that the association was not limited to people who frequently used cannabis. It also appeared across different methods of consumption (smoked or edible, etc.). Researchers emphasized that cannabis use should be considered when discussing heart health and stroke prevention.

Scientific Sessions 2026 took place November 6 through 9 in Chicago, bringing together cardiovascular researchers and healthcare professionals from around the world to share scientific discoveries, clinical advances, and emerging evidence.

Cannabis refers to the plant itself, while marijuana is a commonly used term for cannabis products containing enough THC to produce psychoactive effects.

Marijuana Use Is Rising Across the United States.

"Previous research has indicated that cannabis use is rapidly increasing in the United States, with 1 in 6 adults in 2024 reporting having used it within the last month, up from 1 in 10 in 2020 -- a 51% increase," mentioned study author Aabha Divya, M.B.B.S., M.Ch., an assistant professor in the division of cardiothoracic surgery at the Tulane University School of Medicine in New Orleans.

Earlier research conducted between 2016 and 2020 had already identified associations between cannabis consumption and unfavorable cardiovascular outcomes. Those findings also suggested that using cannabis more frequently during a given month was connected to greater cardiovascular risk.

Recent findings suggest that however, the evidence has not always been consistent. With recreational marijuana becoming legal in more places and cannabis products increasingly available, Divya and colleagues wanted to investigate these possible health effects in a larger population.

In a recent development, "We wanted to expand on this earlier work because cannabis use has become increasingly common in the United States, as recreational legalization and commercial availability of various products with cannabis have also expanded. Previous studies have raised concerns about possible cardiovascular effects; however, the results have not been consistent," Divya remarked.

The researchers examined information collected through the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS), a large telephone survey of American adults. They combined responses from jurisdictions that collected information about cannabis consumption between 2020 and 2024.

Participants answered questions about their marijuana use and whether a healthcare professional had ever diagnosed them with cardiovascular conditions, including a heart attack, stroke, or coronary heart disease.

Even Occasional Marijuana Use Was Linked to Higher Stroke Odds.

It has been revealed that one of the most striking findings was that infrequent cannabis use was associated with cardiovascular problems. In fact, the researchers did not find the steady increase in cardiovascular risk with more frequent use that they had expected.

The analysis revealed several key associations:.

These findings were unexpected because the relationship between cannabis use and cardiovascular disease did not consistently become stronger as consumption increased.

"We were surprised to find that the link between cannabis use and cardiovascular disease was not straightforward. We expected that the chances of heart disease would gradually rise as people used cannabis more often, but that wasn't the case. Both low-use and heavy-use groups had higher odds of developing heart disease," Divya noted.

Although the study cannot establish that marijuana directly causes strokes or other cardiovascular conditions, the findings suggest that occasional consumption should not automatically be considered free of potential cardiovascular concerns.

"As cannabis use becomes more common, it is increasingly important that people and their healthcare professionals include it in conversations about cardiovascular health, just as they discuss tobacco, alcohol and other commonly used substances," she added.

Experts Urge Greater Attention to Cannabis and Heart Health.

Recent findings suggest that robert L. Page II, Pharm.D., M.S.P.H., FAHA, who led the writing group responsible for the American Heart Association's 2020 cannabis scientific statement, stated the findings add to growing concerns about marijuana's possible cardiovascular effects.

One challenge in evaluating those effects is that many cannabis owners also smoke tobacco. Because tobacco is already an established cardiovascular risk factor, separating its effects from those of cannabis can be difficult.

Page, who was not involved in the research, explained why the new findings deserve attention.

"Unfortunately, many patients who use cannabis may also smoke tobacco, which completely clouds the problem when addressing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk. In patients who use both, cannabis has always been considered an innocent bystander; however, this is not the case. This is the second observational study to suggest that cannabis exposure (without tobacco smoking) may be a potential risk factor for developing cardiovascular disease. Overall, cannabis is beginning to emerge as a major contributor to premature heart disease in young and older adults, which can lead to serious cardiovascular events. To this end, clinicians should be addressing cannabis use with their patients as they would tobacco use when considering the risk of cardiovascular disease.".

Page is a professor in the department of clinical pharmacy and the department of physical medicine/rehabilitation at the University of Colorado Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences in Aurora, Colorado.

How Researchers Studied Nearly Half a Million Americans.

The analysis included 442,906 adults living in the United States (average age of 49 years; approximately half women). Their responses came from telephone surveys conducted through the BRFSS.

Researchers used survey information collected from 2020 through 2024, focusing on states that had included an optional marijuana questionnaire. Between 16 and 24 states participated in this portion of the survey each year, meaning the analysis did not represent every state.

Industry observers note that participants reported how many days they had consumed cannabis during the preceding month. The questions covered multiple ways of using marijuana (smoking, vaping or ingesting gummies or other cannabis-containing foods).

The researchers divided participants into four categories based on their reported use:.

Participants also indicated whether they had ever received a diagnosis of heart attack, heart disease, heart-related chest pain, or stroke.

To better distinguish the association with cannabis from other potential explanations, the researchers accounted for numerous established cardiovascular risk factors. These included demographic characteristics, tobacco smoking, alcohol consumption, obesity, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, physical inactivity, education, and income.

Why the Findings Do Not Prove Marijuana Causes Strokes.

Despite the large number of participants, the study has several limitations that affect how its findings should be interpreted.

First, the analysis examined associations between reported cannabis use and previously diagnosed cardiovascular conditions at a single point in time. This means researchers could not determine whether marijuana use preceded the cardiovascular problems or whether it directly contributed to them.

The information also depended on participants accurately recalling and reporting their cannabis consumption and medical histories (making them subject to potential errors in memory). Such reports may not always reflect actual patterns of use or diagnoses.

Another limitation was the lack of information about the strength of the cannabis products participants consumed or the quantities they used. Without those details, the researchers could not evaluate whether THC potency or the amount consumed influenced the observed associations.

Sources indicate that the researchers also acknowledged that some participants may have reduced or discontinued cannabis consumption after being diagnosed with cardiovascular disease. As a result, the group reporting no cannabis use in the previous month may have included former users.

These uncertainties make it difficult to draw firm conclusions about how consumption frequency affects cardiovascular health. Nevertheless, the findings add to growing evidence that cannabis use deserves closer examination as a possible factor in heart disease and stroke.

As marijuana becomes more widely available and its use continues to increase, researchers and healthcare professionals are emphasizing the importance of discussing cannabis alongside other substances that may affect cardiovascular health.

This isn’t Broderdorf’s first time at Dodge. He’s held seven different positions related to marketing, sales, product planning, and operations throughout his 25-year tenure at Stellantis. Dodge has been led by Matt McAlear since 2024, but McAlear has been spread thin at Stellantis since February, when he took over as Chrysler’s CEO and head of Alfa Romeo North America. McAleer will now focus solely on Chrysler, which is expected to release three fresh models in the next few years.

Chrysler’s lineup currently consists of just the Pacifica minivan. However, the brand has already announced the Airflow, a upcoming compact SUV slated to launch in 2028 and start at less than $40,000, and is also working on the Arrow and Arrow Cross, which will come in under $30,000.Both CEOs will report to Tim Kuniskis, who assumes a new role as U.S. chief commercial officer. Kuniskis joined Stellantis in 1992 and served in several leadership roles before retiring from his position as head of Dodge and Ram in May 2024.

Retirement only lasted about seven months, though, and Kuniskis reportedly said he was “bored to death” after about two weeks out of work. By December 2024, Stellantis had announced Kuniskis’s appointment as Ram’s CEO. Since his return, Kuniskis has passed the Ram brand to Matt VanDyke and has taken over as head of American Brands, North America Marketing, SRT, and Stellantis’s Direct Connection parts division.

In a recent development, now, Kuniskis adds U.S. retail, fleet sales, and the dealer network to his long list of leadership divisions following the departure of Michael Orange, former senior vice president of U.S. sales and network performance. Kuniskis will report to Stellantis North America’s chief operating officer, Pablo Di Si, who was appointed to the role earlier this month.

Dodge is expected to stuff a supercharged V-8 back into the Charger for the 2028 model year, while Chevy is gearing up to bring back the Camaro around 2028. The only other V-8-powered car under $100,000 is the Corvette, which has a completely different form factor with its mid-engine layout, but it will likely still be cross-shopped against the Cobra.

Pricing is probably the biggest risk. Ford needs to make sure it doesn’t alienate its customers by making it too expensive, given that the Dark Horse SC already has a hefty $105,585 asking price (about $20K more than the GT500 that it replaced). The new 5.4-liter V-8 will also have to make a strong impression as a successor to the much-loved Voodoo.

Sources indicate that the Mustang Cobra will likely be revealed in early 2027 and go on sale before the end of the year. We expect pricing to start somewhere in the $80,000 range, but it could easily climb to $100,000 for a Cobra R model.

#5053. Energy drinks linked to 11 times more reports of cardiac arrest

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1381 w)

Energy drinks linked to 11 times more reports of cardiac arrest

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1381 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that energy drinks and stimulant supplements are raising latest concerns about heart health after researchers discovered a striking pattern in reports of serious cardiovascular emergencies.
  • Industry observers note that the findings were particularly concerning among younger adults.
  • Researchers emphasized that the findings do not establish that energy drinks or stimulant supplements caused these medical emergencies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that energy drinks and stimulant supplements are raising latest concerns about heart health after researchers discovered a striking pattern in reports of serious cardiovascular emergencies. Products containing caffeine and other stimulants appeared far more frequently in reports of cardiac arrest, heart attacks, and other heart problems than products without these ingredients.

Industry observers note that the findings were particularly concerning among younger adults. People ages 18 to 34 accounted for a substantial share of the reported heart problems involving caffeinated products, according to independent, preliminary research presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026.

Researchers emphasized that the findings do not establish that energy drinks or stimulant supplements caused these medical emergencies. However, the unusually high frequency of certain cardiovascular events in FDA safety reports suggests that these widely available products deserve closer examination.

Growing Concerns About Energy Drinks and Heart Health.

The energy drink industry has expanded rapidly, with sales more than doubling over the past decade and exceeding $20 billion in 2024. Despite their popularity, scientists still have limited information about the cardiovascular effects of energy drinks and supplements containing stimulants.

Sources indicate that existing evidence suggests that consuming large amounts of caffeine can harm the cardiovascular system. Medical professionals have also documented cases of arrhythmias (irregular heart rhythms) and sudden cardiac death following the consumption of these products. Some of these incidents involved young adults who had no previously identified risk factors for heart disease.

A 2026 American Heart Association Scientific Statement on caffeine and cardiovascular disease indicates that most adults can generally consume up to 400 mg of caffeine daily without significant safety concerns (the equivalent of up to 5, 8-ounce cups of regular black caffeinated coffee).

It has been revealed that however, caffeine concentrations can differ dramatically between products. Certain energy drinks provide up to three times as much caffeine per fluid ounce as brewed coffee, while some pre-workout supplements contain more than 12 times the concentration found in coffee.

Sources indicate that another concern involves how these products are regulated. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) classifies energy drinks and stimulant supplements as foods or dietary supplements rather than medications. As a result, they are not subject to the same safety testing requirements that medications must meet before entering the market.

"These products are marketed as everyday pick-me-ups and sold next to soda and bottled water, so most people assume they carry no real risk," said study author Sai Samayamanthula, a fourth-year medical student at the University of Virginia School of Medicine in Charlottesville, Virginia. "For many healthy people, if these products are consumed occasionally, the risk is probably small. However, individuals who consume energy drinks or other stimulant-containing supplements regularly can promptly exceed the recommended daily limit for caffeine, so it's important for people to know that there may be a risk of cardiovascular harm with these products.".

FDA Reports Reveal Striking Differences in Cardiac Events.

To investigate possible cardiovascular safety concerns, researchers examined a federal database containing reports of suspected adverse reactions to foods and dietary supplements. They compared products containing caffeine and other stimulants with products that did not contain these ingredients.

According to recent reports, the comparison group included commonly consumed products such as soft drinks, smoothies, vitamins, protein bars, and meal replacement shakes. Researchers examined reports involving people ages 13 and older submitted between 2017 and 2025.

Several differences stood out in the analysis:.

These differences describe how frequently certain medical problems appeared within the FDA reports. They do not mean that people consuming energy drinks face an 11 times greater actual risk of cardiac arrest or a 4.5 times greater risk of having a heart attack.

Recent findings suggest that "Our findings support the case for more systematic safety monitoring of caffeine- and stimulant-containing products. In addition, healthcare professionals should remember to ask their younger patients who have palpitations, chest pain, or fainting spells if they recently or regularly consume these products," Samayamanthula said.

Why Young Adults May Be Particularly Vulnerable.

One of the most notable findings was the large proportion of cardiovascular reports involving younger adults. Researchers have not yet determined why the connection between stimulant products and reported heart problems appeared so frequently in this age group.

Sources indicate that several explanations are possible. Younger consumers may use energy drinks and stimulant supplements more often, increasing the likelihood that these products appear in reports of medical emergencies.

According to recent reports, how the products are consumed could also influence the pattern. Potential contributing factors include the circumstances surrounding their use (for example, consuming them before intense exercise or mixing them with alcohol or drugs). Some individuals may also have previously undiagnosed heart conditions that could make them more susceptible to cardiovascular complications.

These possibilities remain uncertain, and additional research will be needed to determine which factors, if any, help explain the unusually high reporting frequency among younger adults.

Do Energy Drinks Actually Cause Heart Attacks?

Although the results raise notable questions about products containing concentrated caffeine and other stimulants, experts caution against interpreting the findings as proof of a direct cause.

In a recent development, "This study raises concerns that products with very high amounts of caffeine may be harmful to the cardiovascular system," stated Gregory M. Marcus, M.D., M.A.S., FAHA, chair of the 2026 American Heart Association scientific statement on caffeine and cardiovascular disease. "Although there are biological reasons why that connection could be possible, the study does not prove that caffeine products cause these events, because other factors may have influenced the results found in this analysis. More research is needed to understand whether these stimulant products are truly responsible for the reported heart-related events.".

Marcus did not participate in the research. He is a professor of medicine at the University of California, San Francisco School of Medicine and serves as associate chief of the Cardiology for Research program at the University of California, San Francisco Health.

Because the analysis relied on reports submitted voluntarily to the FDA, it cannot establish whether the products themselves were responsible for the cardiovascular events. Other health conditions, behaviors, or circumstances may have played a role.

How Researchers Analyzed the FDA Safety Reports.

The research team reviewed 28,345 reports of possible adverse events submitted to an FDA safety database from 2017 through 2025.

It has been revealed that of these, 854 reports involved energy drinks or dietary supplements containing caffeine or other stimulants. The remaining 27,491 reports concerned products without caffeine or stimulant ingredients and served as the comparison group.

It has been revealed that researchers classified products according to the ingredients they contained. The stimulant category included caffeine, methylxanthines (theobromine, guarana, yerba mate, green tea/coffee extracts) and sympathomimetics (synephrine, yohimbine, ephedra, DMAA, higenamine).

Sources indicate that rather than evaluating individual brands, the researchers grouped products by their ingredients. Consequently, the findings apply to broad categories of caffeinated and stimulant products and do not identify any particular brand as more dangerous than another.

In a recent development, the researchers also highlighted notable limitations in the available data. Reports were voluntarily submitted by members of the public, consumers, healthcare professionals, and manufacturers, meaning that the database does not provide a complete record of everyone who experienced a possible adverse reaction.

Just as importantly, the researchers could not determine how many people consumed these products without developing cardiovascular problems. They also could not establish how many people experienced heart problems but never submitted a report.

Without those figures, the analysis cannot calculate the actual likelihood of a heart attack, cardiac arrest, or another cardiovascular event among consumers of energy drinks and stimulant supplements.

It has been revealed that nevertheless, the findings reveal a potentially key safety signal. Researchers say more systematic monitoring and further studies are needed to determine whether these products contribute directly to serious heart problems, particularly among younger adults who frequently consume them.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.
  • Recent findings suggest that patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller enhancement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Recent findings suggest that patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller enhancement. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

Industry observers note that the patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a substantial focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

Recent findings suggest that the end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Sources indicate that interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

It has been revealed that the other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Sources indicate that finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

Read on below for the 1.1.3.5 change log.

In a recent development, the Valhalla is motivated by a massively powerful plug-in hybrid powertrain. At its core is a Mercedes-AMG–sourced twin-turbo 4.0-liter V-8 with a flat-plane crank. It feeds the rear wheels through an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission and apportions torque via an electronically controlled limited-slip rear differential. Additionally, two electric motors power the front wheels and a third is integrated into the transmission. Combined output is 1064 horsepower.

Sources indicate that lightweight carbon fiber makes up the car's core structure. The Valhalla also features F1-style pushrod front suspension and employs a multi-link setup at the rear. Adaptive dampers and carbon-ceramic brakes are standard. Active aerodynamics are a major feature of the Valhalla, with movable front and rear wings that adjust to balance downforce and drag, maximize grip, and improve braking performance. When we drove the Valhalla, we found it to be remarkably engaging to drive for such a powerful, high-tech machine, more friendly on the road than you'd expect.

According to recent reports, blinkie is, simply put, a pink ghost. He's just as lost as you are, but he seems to have an opinion on everything you encounter out in the big, wide world, which is definitely welcome given how adorable he is. That said, he also adds a nice little touch in making you feel not-so-alone while venturing out into the unknown, as that's basically what you'll be doing in Cauldron.

The world is divided into blocks, with those you haven't explored greyed out, similar to the fog of war. You'll need to battle all sorts of monsters in the dark to clear up that area, with each one telling you whether or not the area is too strong for you to take on.

That, of course, adds to the motivation to grind until I can smack those little slime monsters out of the way, which can be done via the little minigames that increase your stats as you go along. You can fish, catch apples, and even mine for treasure, all while encountering and freeing party mates with distinct skills in the process.

It's a compelling loop that, while nothing groundbreaking, manages to capture what makes RPGs so great in their distilled form - and the fact that it's on mobile makes it even easier to pick up and play anytime. So, how do you play Cauldron: The Minigame RPG? As always in this series, Cauldron: The Minigame RPG is in early access on Google Play, where you can give it a go for free before committing to a full purchase. Knowing Snapbreak, I don't think it's going to take too long before it's officially released into the wild, but if you fancy dipping in before anyone else, now's your chance!

Walking and weight training may not be enough to keep your bones strong

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (884 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The type of exercise you do may be more key for your bones than how long you spend doing it.
  • Sources indicate that the findings, published in Sports Medicine - Open, suggest that certain fast-paced sports may provide greater benefits for bone metabolism than walking or conventional strength training.
  • To investigate how different forms of exercise affect bones, the Semmelweis University team reviewed 24 clinical studies involving 1,238 healthy adults.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The type of exercise you do may be more key for your bones than how long you spend doing it. Researchers at Semmelweis University have found that intense physical activity involving sudden bursts of movement, quick changes in direction, and sharp turns appears especially effective at stimulating new bone formation.

Sources indicate that the findings, published in Sports Medicine - Open, suggest that certain fast-paced sports may provide greater benefits for bone metabolism than walking or conventional strength training. The research could help scientists develop more effective exercise recommendations for preserving bone health and reducing the risk of osteoporosis.

Why Exercise Intensity Matters for Bone Health.

To investigate how different forms of exercise affect bones, the Semmelweis University team reviewed 24 clinical studies involving 1,238 healthy adults.

Industry observers note that instead of relying on bone mineral density measurements, which can take considerable time to reveal changes, the researchers examined blood markers associated with the production of new bone tissue. These biological indicators can reveal how bones respond to exercise within a matter of weeks, allowing scientists to detect changes much sooner.

It has been revealed that "What makes our study unique is that we examined not only the type of exercise - whether endurance, resistance, or combined training - but also exercise intensity, frequency, and duration. Our goal was to determine which forms of exercise stimulate bone metabolism most effectively and which appear to be less beneficial from this perspective," mentioned Dr. Péter Ferdinandy, Vice-Rector for Science and Innovations at Semmelweis University and senior author of the study.

Football and Handball Show Surprising Bone Benefits.

The strongest responses were associated with vigorous sports that repeatedly require players to accelerate, change direction, turn, and make powerful movements.

Recreational football and handball stood out in particular. These activities were linked to increases of up to 45-46 percent in blood markers associated with bone formation, suggesting that they may provide a particularly strong stimulus for the body's bone-building processes.

Industry observers note that more conventional activities generally produced smaller responses. Walking, step aerobics, and standard resistance workouts performed in the gym were less effective at stimulating the measured indicators of bone formation.

The findings were especially unexpected for resistance training, which is commonly recommended as a way to support skeletal health.

It has been revealed that "The most surprising finding was that resistance training did not produce a significant effect on markers of bone metabolism, even though several professional guidelines recommend this type of exercise for maintaining bone health. Likewise, low- or moderate-intensity endurance exercise, such as walking or jogging, indicated no meaningful long-term effect," explained Viktória Barna, PhD student at Semmelweis University and first author of the study.

Why Walking and Weight Training Still Matter.

The results do not suggest that walking, jogging, or other less demanding activities should be abandoned. These forms of exercise continue to offer important health benefits, even if they do not stimulate the measured bone-building processes as strongly as more intense sports.

Rather, the research indicates that maintaining healthy bones may require greater mechanical stimulation than many everyday activities provide. Movements that place more substantial forces on the skeleton appear to produce a stronger response in the biological processes involved in forming upcoming bone.

However, the researchers stress that people should not suddenly begin strenuous exercise without preparing appropriately.

This is especially vital for individuals with cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, or metabolic conditions, as well as those who already have osteoporosis. Anyone in these groups who is considering a new activity or a more physically demanding exercise routine should first speak with their treating physician, general practitioner, or a sports medicine specialist. Medical guidance can help determine whether the activity and its intensity are suitable for their health and physical capabilities.

Could High-Intensity Exercise Help Prevent Osteoporosis?

Sources indicate that the findings offer a new perspective on how exercise could be used to maintain bone health as people age. While the analysis focused on markers of bone metabolism rather than direct changes in bone density, the results suggest that vigorous activity may encourage early biological changes that support bone formation.

It has been revealed that "According to the World Health Organization, regular physical activity offers numerous health benefits. However, our findings suggest that low-intensity exercise alone is not sufficient to stimulate bone metabolism. High-intensity exercise may trigger early beneficial changes in bone formation, potentially helping to slow bone loss and support healthy aging," summarized Dr. Nóra Sydó, clinical specialist and co-author of the study.

The researchers believe that understanding which movements most effectively stimulate bone formation could lead to better exercise programs designed to preserve skeletal strength and help prevent osteoporosis.

For now, the findings highlight an vital distinction: staying physically active is beneficial for overall health, but keeping bones healthy over the long term may depend not only on how much people move, but also on how powerfully and dynamically they move.

It has been revealed that the collector-car world is filled with all types of blue-chip sure bets, but the way traffic looked in the past isn't well represented by what you might find on the lawn at Pebble Beach today. Instead, the roads of the past were filled with plainer cars, most of which don't survive the erosion of time.

It has been revealed that however, a special example of a very ordinary little car has just turned up on Bring a Trailer (which, like Car and Driver, is part of Hearst Autos). It’s a 1986 Yugo GT with only 121 miles on the odometer. You have to have a sense of humor to keep a collector-grade Yugo around, and in this case, the previous owner clearly did, as he was the producer behind such screwball comedies as the second Ace Ventura movie and Major League II.

See all results for used cars for sale near 20147.

Recent findings suggest that baltimore's James G. Robinson founded Morgan Creek Entertainment, running it as a successful movie production tech giant for decades. Not every movie it made was Oscar-winning material, but there were plenty of hits along the way. Robin Hood: Prince of Thieves was something of a pincushion for critical arrows, but it ended up as the second-highest-grossing movie of 1991.

Robinson died earlier this year, having amassed a collection of more than 100 cars, some of them obviously collector grade, like a Mercedes 300SL roadster. Among such vaunted company, this little Yugo might have seemed like a donkey in a barn full of thoroughbreds, but it has a pretty special story of its own.

It has been revealed that along with his Hollywood work, Robinson was also involved in the automotive trade, prepping imported cars after shipment from Europe, and even installing U.S.-grade air conditioning systems. His manufacturer processed many of the imported Yugos, and he was friends with the importer Malcolm Bricklin.

Like a movie panned by the critics, the Yugo was derided as cheap and disposable and was often the butt of jokes. Really, it offered honest, if basic, transportation for not much money. Based on the Fiat 128, it was produced in Yugoslavia by the former arms manufacturer Zastava and brought to the U.S. market in 1985 by Bricklin, who also gets credit for introducing Subaru to America.

Sources indicate that featuring a simple and practical hatchback layout, this Yugo GV comes with a 1.1-liter four-cylinder engine good for just 55 horsepower. The layout is fairly bare-bones, but you do get a cassette deck, air conditioning, and a roof rack. This Yugo also runs disc brakes up front and 13-inch wheels at each corner.

See all results for used cars for sale near 20147.

It has been revealed that more than 140,000 Yugos were sold in the U.S., with nearly 800,000 in total global production. Though the car was never a critical hit, those figures nonetheless make this little hatchback a commercial success. Like the films Mr. Robinson produced, it was a crowd pleaser.

Such a clean, low-mileage example with a great connection to the Yugo story is something that probably belongs in a museum. However, the cost of entry is likely to be low enough that the car could be driven sparingly and displayed at the odd car show. It may never get past the velvet rope for the Pebble Beach Concours, but show up at next year's Monterey Car Week in a Yugo this pristine, and heads will turn.

#5041. Tech Report: Colorectal cancer is rising again after 20 years, and scientists don't know why

📅 12 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1554 w)

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Colorectal cancer is rising again after 20 years, and scientists don't know why

📅 12 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1554 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that colorectal cancer rates are climbing again in the United States after more than two decades of decline, and the troubling increase is affecting far more than younger adults.
  • Industry observers note that colorectal cancer is already the second leading cause of cancer deaths in the United States and the leading cause among adults younger than 50.
  • Colorectal Cancer Rates Reverse Decades of Decline.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that colorectal cancer rates are climbing again in the United States after more than two decades of decline, and the troubling increase is affecting far more than younger adults. New research published in NEJM Evidence reveals that the disease is becoming more common across nearly every age group under 70, raising concerns about a growing public health challenge.

Industry observers note that colorectal cancer is already the second leading cause of cancer deaths in the United States and the leading cause among adults younger than 50. Although rising cases in younger people have attracted widespread attention, the latest findings show that the problem extends into older generations. Researchers warn that a continued increase could place additional pressure on the healthcare system as more patients require cancer treatment and long-term care after diagnosis.

Colorectal Cancer Rates Reverse Decades of Decline.

It has been revealed that to investigate the changing pattern, Caitlin Murphy, PhD, MPH, Professor of Pediatrics and Public Health Sciences at the University of Chicago, and her colleagues examined the latest colorectal cancer incidence data from the National Cancer Institute. Their analysis tracked changes in diagnoses from 2000 through 2023.

In a recent development, the results revealed a significant reversal. In 2000, the age-adjusted colorectal cancer incidence rate was 55.2 cases per 100,000 people. By 2022, that figure had dropped to 36.7. However, the rate increased to 38.3 in 2023, marking the first overall rise after more than two decades of falling rates.

"This is the first time that we have seen an increase in the overall rate since in more than 20 years," Murphy said. She emphasized that the long-standing downward trend had been a major feature of colorectal cancer statistics for decades. The new analysis indicates that rates are now increasing in every age group through ages 65 to 69.

Murphy, an epidemiologist who specializes in colorectal cancer patterns, had anticipated that the increase initially observed in younger adults would eventually become apparent among older people. She attributes this expected progression to a phenomenon called the "birth cohort effect.".

In a recent development, this effect describes how people born during the same general period can share risk patterns that become more apparent as they grow older. In this case, individuals born in the 1960s and subsequent decades appear to face an elevated risk of colorectal cancer as they enter middle age and later life.

"I think of a birth cohort effect as the interaction of age and time," Murphy explained. "As people born around the same time move through time and age together, we're going to see more colorectal cancers being diagnosed.".

A Sharp Increase Among Adults Ages 45 to 49.

One of the most striking findings involved people between 45 and 49 years old. From 2019 through 2023, colorectal cancer incidence in this group increased by 12.76% annually, the largest rise recorded among the age groups examined.

Recent findings suggest that researchers believe much of this particular increase can be explained by changes in cancer screening recommendations. National guidelines lowered the recommended starting age for routine colorectal cancer screening from 50 to 45, allowing more people to be tested and more previously undetected cancers to be identified.

"That means that screening is doing as we intend it to do -- it's catching cancer earlier," Murphy stated.

But increased screening cannot account for the broader pattern. Colorectal cancer rates are also rising among adults ages 65 to 69, while the decline has stalled among those ages 70 to 74. Both populations have historically experienced substantial benefits from screening, and approximately 80% of people in these age groups are current with recommended testing.

These findings are particularly concerning because they suggest that additional, unidentified risk factors could be counteracting some of the progress achieved through decades of cancer screening.

The research team also investigated whether disruptions during the COVID-19 pandemic might have distorted the results. Cancer screenings and diagnoses were affected during the pandemic, potentially changing when cases were detected. However, the upward trend remained even after the researchers removed data from 2020 and 2021. Screening activity had also largely recovered to its earlier levels by January 2021, making pandemic-related disruptions an unlikely explanation for the increase recorded in 2023.

"These results motivate us to understand reasons for this rise, so risk factors can be identified and possibly reduced," stated Sonia Kupfer, MD, director of the Gastrointestinal Cancer Risk and Prevention Clinic at UChicago Medicine.

Why Colorectal Cancer Is Rising Across Generations.

Sources indicate that the growing number of colorectal cancer diagnoses among younger Americans has become a major health concern. American Cancer Society data show that incidence among adults ages 20 to 49 increased by approximately 3% per year between 2013 and 2022.

This increase in colorectal cancer among people younger than 50, often referred to as early-onset colorectal cancer, has drawn considerable public and scientific attention. The latest study suggests that understanding why younger adults are developing the disease more frequently could also help explain what is happening in older populations.

Sources indicate that "There are many unique challenges when you're diagnosed with cancer at a young age, so it's notable that we shine a spotlight on that problem," Murphy said. "But in terms of understanding the root cause, I think our study shows that we can consider that whatever might be causing colorectal cancer in younger people is now also causing it to increase in older people as well.".

The underlying causes remain uncertain, but researchers are investigating whether exposure to chemicals in the environment could play a role.

Murphy and her colleagues are working with Xin Hu, PhD, a toxicologist at Emory University, to examine this possibility. Their approach involves analyzing small blood samples for evidence of thousands of environmental chemical exposures simultaneously. By identifying which substances are associated with potential risks, the team hopes to narrow the list of chemicals that deserve more detailed investigation.

The researchers then plan to collaborate with Kupfer to explore how these chemicals affect colon tissue. To do so, they will use organoids, laboratory-grown models that reproduce important features of the colon. These miniature tissue systems allow scientists to study biological responses in a controlled environment and could help uncover how certain exposures contribute to colorectal cancer.

Why Colorectal Cancer Screening Remains Critical.

With cancer rates increasing across a broad range of ages, the researchers emphasize the need to keep tracking national cancer statistics as fresh registry information becomes available each year.

Murphy cautions that the consequences could become substantial if the current pattern continues. As large numbers of Americans born in more recent decades grow older, rising incidence rates could translate into many additional cancer diagnoses. That would increase demand for medical treatment and services supporting people who survive colorectal cancer.

While scientists work to understand the factors behind the increase, screening remains one of the most effective ways to find colorectal cancer early and reduce the risk of dying from the disease.

In a recent development, current national recommendations advise adults at average risk to begin regular colorectal cancer screening at age 45 and continue through age 75. For people younger than 45 or older than 75, screening decisions should be tailored to individual circumstances, including family medical history, symptoms, and other health conditions.

Colonoscopy continues to be considered the gold standard for colorectal cancer screening, but patients also have additional testing options. These include newer blood-based screening tests and stool tests that can be completed at home.

"There are several ways to do screening that should be discussed with a clinician, so people know what the different screening tests are intended for and how often these need to be repeated," Kupfer added.

She also stressed that people younger than 45 should not ignore possible warning signs simply because they have not reached the age recommended for routine screening. Those without known genetic or family history risk factors should still seek medical attention if they notice blood in their stool, persistent changes in bowel habits, or unexplained weight loss.

Study Funding and Future Cancer Research.

The research, titled "Colorectal cancer among U.S. adults, 2000-2023," received financial support from the National Institutes of Health and the Eli and Edythe Broad Center of Regenerative Medicine and Stem Cell Research Ablon Scholars Program.

Along with Murphy, the study's authors include Folasade P. May of the University of California Los Angeles, Xin Hu of Emory University in Atlanta, and Samir Gupta of the University of California San Diego.

The University of Chicago's medical and biological sciences programs are also continuing to expand their work in cancer research and patient care. In April 2027, UChicago Medicine is scheduled to open the AbbVie Foundation Cancer Pavilion, which will be Chicago's first freestanding cancer pavilion. The facility is intended to bring together advanced diagnostic services, latest cancer treatments, research that translates laboratory discoveries into clinical care, and comprehensive support for patients and the surrounding community.
