Breaking: 10 Great Games That Defined The Xbox 360

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1503 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • November 2026 will see the original Xbox consoles and the overall Xbox brand celebrate its 25th anniversary.
  • Without a doubt, the most prosperous era of the Xbox brand was that of the Xbox 360, as it was not only the go-to home console for hardcore gamers of the time but the 360 was also home to numerous innovative exclusive titles, software, and hardware.
  • In celebration of the Xbox’s brand’s 25th anniversary, here’s a look back at 10 exclusive Xbox 360 games that defined the console and Microsoft’s brief time at the top of the gaming market.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

November 2026 will see the original Xbox consoles and the overall Xbox brand celebrate its 25th anniversary. and while many gamers will surely be reminiscing their time playing on the sixth gen console, this month should also be a time to celebrate Xbox’s other eras.

Without a doubt, the most prosperous era of the Xbox brand was that of the Xbox 360, as it was not only the go-to home console for hardcore gamers of the time but the 360 was also home to numerous innovative exclusive titles, software, and hardware.

In celebration of the Xbox’s brand’s 25th anniversary, here’s a look back at 10 exclusive Xbox 360 games that defined the console and Microsoft’s brief time at the top of the gaming market.

As mentioned before, the 360 era was a very experimental era for Xbox hardware and this was best represented by the innovative hands-free motion capture camera sensor, the Kinect, with arguably its most famous game being Kinect Star Wars.

In many ways, the Kinect was Microsoft’s answer to the Nintendo Wii and to help compete against the Wii, Microsoft published several promising motion titles such as Kinect Star Wars, allowing people to play a Jedi, Podrace, and wreak chaos as a Rancor all with just their hand and body movements.

Sure, Kinect Star Wars has become sort of a joke over the years, thanks in large part to its Just Dance-like Galactic Dance Off, but it’s still arguably the best game on the 360 to showcase the potential and capabilities of the Kinect.

It has been revealed that project Gotham Racing and Forza Motorsport were the go-to exclusive racing games for Xbox players for several years. While they were fun, neither series allowed players to freely drive in an open-world, an glitch Microsoft chose to rectify in the Forza spinoff game Forza Horizon.

Set in Colorado during the Horizon Festival street racing event, Forza Horizon had players take part in the Festival’s formal street races using over 200 cars, as well as challenge other players and even planes and helicopters to informal races throughout the state.

This free style racing design and its vast array of customization options made Forza Horizon an instant hit, leading developer Playground Games to create multiple Horizon sequels and even eclipse Motorsport to become Xbox’s definitive exclusive racing franchise.

In 2002, Microsoft acquired the beloved British game developer Rare for $375 million, and while they would only release two games for the original Xbox, they would develop several titles exclusively for the Xbox 360. Arguably the best was Viva Piñata.

A first-person life simulation game, Viva Piñata was one of the most unique titles offered exclusively on the 360, as it centered around players restoring a garden on Piñata Island to attract adorable local piñata-themed animals to farm, breed, and defend before ultimately sending them to parties.

Viva Piñata is still to this very day widely considered to be the best upcoming IP Rare created under Microsoft, and while the series has laid dormant for years following the release of a sequel and two spinoffs, it's still fondly remembered by many for its creative designs, comedy, and unique gameplay routine.

Sources indicate that one of the best exclusive original Xbox RPGs was Lionhead Studios’ Fable. Sadly, it didn’t completely live up to series creator Peter Molyneux’s claims and hype, though the series would slowly start to achieve all of Molyneux’s promises in the sequel, Fable II.

Set roughly 500 years after the first game in a newly industrial iteration of Albion, Fable II has players embody an orphan known as Sparrow as they grow to become a newly introduced hero, destined to save Albion from the ruthless Lord Lucien.

As of this writing, Fable II is Fable at its best, as not only does it feature an intriguing fantasy, industrial world but it features several latest and immersive mechanics such as a permanent dog companion, flintlock style firearms, local and online two-player co-op, and allowing players to have children.

Industry observers note that the Xbox 360 wasn’t as powerful as the PlayStation 3 on paper, but the Microsoft console was far easier to develop games for than the Sony platform, leading many companies to develop their titles exclusively for the 360. One such game was Capcom’s Dead Rising.

Zombie games had been common for a while by the time of Dead Rising’s 2006 launch, but DR was the first zombie game to properly depict massive zombie hordes that had only appeared in books and films beforehand, with literally thousands of zombies filling the Willamette Mall.

On top of these huge herds of the undead, Dead Rising further showcased the power of the 360 by allowing the game’s protagonist, Frank West, to slay zombies with practically every object found in the mall, such as jugs of orange juice, CDs, katanas, shopping carts, lawnmowers, and more.

BioWare and Microsoft formed a strong relationship during the original Xbox era by releasing Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic and Jade Empire exclusively for the sixth gen console. This relationship continued briefly into the 360 era, with the launch of Mass Effect.

Inspired by Star Wars, Mass Effect was BioWare’s most ambitious project, as it introduced several latest mechanics that have since become mainstays in RPGs, such as real-time, third-person, cover-focused combat, conversational Dialogue Wheel choices, and NPC relationships that would continue into future sequels.

With its expansive sci-fi universe, memorable characters, and easy to understand gameplay, Mass Effect continued to show that both BioWare and Xbox were the undisputed masters of western RPGs, as the innovations made in ME can still be felt in several RPGs today.

2007 is well known to be one of the best years in gaming history, especially for those who owned an Xbox 360, as that year not only saw the launch of Mass Effect, Crackdown, and Lost Odyssey, but also the debut of a true work of gaming art in the form of BioShock.

Released as a timed 360 exclusive, BioShock was a spiritual successor to the FPS System Shock series. Instead of traveling to a space station, BioShock had players journey to a mysterious lighthouse deep below the sea to a hidden mid-20th century underwater city called Rapture full of ruination.

BioShock’s gameplay was fantastic, but what made it really stand out from other games of its era was its environmental design inspired by gothic and art deco concepts and its haunting narrative full of horrors, despair, and twists around every corner.

While the Xbox Live Arcade digital storefront didn’t debut on the 360, Arcade was at its most popular during the 360 era, launching several hit exclusive titles such as Braid, 'Splosion Man, Shadow Complex, and the storefront’s absolute best-seller, Minecraft.

Long before Microsoft acquired Mojang but shortly after Minecraft first debuted on PCs, the hit cubic sandbox game would make its way to consoles for the first time via Xbox Live Arcade in 2012, in the form of Minecraft: Xbox 360 Edition based on Java Edition Beta 1.6.6.

Since then, Minecraft: Xbox 360 Edition paved the way for millions of console players to easily experience Minecraft for the first time, becoming the source of countless memories of friends exploring an infinite number of worlds, testing out new features in every update, and messing around with Mash-Up packs.

The original Xbox’s defining breakout exclusive title was Halo: Combat Evolved and, in 2006, the 360 would receive its own breakout exclusive game in the form of the third-person cover shooter, Gears of War.

With its innovative third-person gameplay, monstrous Locust enemy designs, and iconic chainsaw bayoneted Lancer assault rifle, Gears of War took the gaming world by storm though everything that made the game great would be significantly improved upon in its sequel, Gears of War 2.

To this day, Gears of War 2 is still considered to feature the best Gears campaign in the series but what it truly revolutionary for gaming overall was the introduction of the PvE Horde Mode pitting players against increasingly deadlier waves of enemies, a mode that many other games would go on to improve upon.

As mentioned before, 2007 was an amazing year for the Xbox 360 but the best exclusive game to debut that year and the one title that undoubtedly best defined the 360 console overall was Bungie’s masterpiece, Halo 3.

The epic conclusion to the original Halo trilogy, Halo 3 saw Master Chief and the Arbiter return to Earth and eventually the Forerunner installation known as the Ark as they and joint UNSC and Elite forces set out to wipe out the Covenant and the Flood once and for all.

Halo 3’s campaign was a perfect finale for the Halo series but Bungie introduced so many fresh features in the game that have made it stand as one of the best FPS titles of all time such as the map editor Forge, Theater Mode, File Share, Grifball, four-player campaign co-op, deployable equipment, and so much more.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that every year since its 50th anniversary in 2018, Hot Wheels has embarked on a worldwide journey to find the ultimate custom car worthy of becoming set in die-cast immortality. The Legends Tour is no joke, and this year’s finalists included a 1961 Morris Minivan transformed into a pickup truck, a custom 1990 NA wide-body Miata, and a bespoke 1992 Chevrolet Salaya SP.

Sources indicate that but above the exotic and the absurd, Matt McEntegart’s custom 1979 Chevrolet El Camino, named the “SS Monte Mino,” brings the trophy home. McEntegart, a Florida native, spent thousands of hours designing and fabricating the build. While the SS Monte Mino wears an El Camino shell, it’s anything but stock, taking parts and inspiration from Corvettes and Monte Carlos.

See all results for Chevrolet Monte Carlo for sale near 79925.

Sources indicate that the SS Monte Mino rides on a modified sixth-generation Corvette chassis. McEntegart stretched the El Camino’s wheelbase by 12 inches and crafted a custom Monte Carlo–inspired wide-body kit using foam prototypes and molds.

The Frankenstein car is powered by a modified Chevy V-8 engine, complete with exposed velocity stacks and performance upgrades. The car practically sits on top of its 22-inch gold wheels thanks to a custom air suspension system.

McEntegart’s low-slung custom ute is a sight to behold, and it truly looks like it was born to speed down a bright orange Hot Wheels track. The exterior is painted in a dark maroon color and uses red-tinted forged carbon-fiber panels to bring out the details along the bodywork.

Inside, the car is all-out retro, with a custom red leather interior to match the exterior red accents. The seats feature a red, black, and gray plaid pattern, and the center console seamlessly blends a few bits of modern tech with the car’s vintage-styled interior.

Industry observers note that the SS Monte Mino will be transformed into a 1:64-scale die-cast Hot Wheels car and join the brand’s Garage of Legends, where it’ll sit among past global winners. The scale model will eventually be available to buy worldwide.

Tesla confirms €3B Cybercab factory at Giga Berlin for up to 1M a year

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1317 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, tesla is going to build the Cybercab in Germany.
  • That’s a lot of robotaxis for a continent where Tesla can’t operate a single one.
  • Plant manager André Thierig announced the decision on X after Tesla told employees on Monday:.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, tesla is going to build the Cybercab in Germany. The company confirmed today a first €3 billion investment in a latest production building at Giga Berlin designed for up to 1 million Cybercabs a year, with production planned for 2029.

That’s a lot of robotaxis for a continent where Tesla can’t operate a single one. Under current EU rules, a driverless vehicle model is capped at 1,500 registrations a year.

Plant manager André Thierig announced the decision on X after Tesla told employees on Monday:.

If you ever wondered, what we would be doing at Giga Berlin with all the land that we have… We are expanding! Cybercab production is coming to Giga Berlin! Today we revealed a first investment of around € 3b in a new manufacturing building with an anticpated start of… pic.twitter.com/vpcDdxoqlW.

Per Tesla’s statement, the €3 billion pays for the new production hall north of the existing plant, plus ancillary buildings and a second wastewater treatment plant. Tesla intends to file the building application before the end of the year, break ground in the first half of 2027, and start production in 2029. The organization claims it will be “the technologically most advanced Tesla factory in the world.”.

Industry observers note that it leaked a few hours earlier. Steven Scholtysek, an automation engineer at the plant, posted that Elon Musk personally signed off on the project last week and that the new hall will be bigger than the original factory.

The building isn’t newly introduced. Tesla laid out a plan to take Giga Berlin to 1 million vehicles a year in its 2023 permit filings and has been clearing land for it since. What’s new is the product. Until today, Tesla had only stated the second hall wouldn’t be another Model Y factory.

Sources indicate that giga Berlin still builds only the Model Y. Tesla has been hiring again at Giga Berlin this year as European demand came back, with a goal of 7,500 cars a week. Even at that pace, the plant would fall short of the 500,000 units a year Tesla promised when it opened in 2022.

Tesla is also adding 4680 battery cell production at the site, with 18 GWh of annual capacity planned.

So the new hall alone is rated for twice what the entire existing plant was supposed to build. And it comes after Musk tied the Berlin expansion to the plant’s works council election in March, warning workers against IG Metall’s influence.

Sources indicate that the EU has a type-approval path for fully driverless vehicles, but it’s a “small series” scheme limited to 1,500 registrations per vehicle type per year across the whole EU. In March, the Commission lifted that cap for automated valet parking. Robotaxis are still stuck in the small-series track.

In a recent development, tesla also has no approval anywhere in Europe for its software to drive without supervision. The Dutch RDW approved the supervised version, now called Tesla Assisted Driving, and nine other countries recognize that approval. It still requires a driver paying attention. The Cybercab has no steering wheel.

Recent findings suggest that rules can move in three years. The Commission has noted it wants large-series approval for other driverless uses, and a UN regulation for automated driving systems is in the works. But as of today, Tesla is committing €3 billion to a vehicle it can’t sell in volume in Europe.

Industry observers note that tesla could export from Berlin, of course. But 1 million Cybercabs a year on top of Giga Texas implies a robotaxi business many times bigger than anything on the road today. Texas, where Cybercab production started in April, had 463 Cybercabs registered as of late October. And Tesla just opened personal Cybercab orders at $29,990 plus a mandatory $299 monthly subscription, usable only inside its Robotaxi geofences.

Recent findings suggest that tesla can’t even launch its driver-assist system in Europe under its own name. What it’s rolling out there isn’t “Full Self-Driving.” It’s “Tesla Assisted Driving,” a level 2 system that needs a driver watching the road at all times, and it took a long fight with regulators to get it approved in 10 countries.

The Cybercab is a much harder sell. No steering wheel, no pedals, so it has to be certified as a level 4 vehicle with nobody inside to take over. That’s a completely different approval from anything Tesla has gotten in Europe. As of this spring, the EU stated no automaker had even used its existing driverless approval path.

Recent findings suggest that and the US program doesn’t inspire confidence. Robotaxi is still confined to geofences, still off highways, and it keeps crashing: Tesla had reported 22 incidents to NHTSA by July, and our analysis of the data earlier this year put it at one crash every 57,000 miles, roughly 9 times worse than the average human driver, with a safety monitor on board. The only reason those crashes don’t get more attention is that they happen at low speed. Of course they do. Tesla keeps the cars on slow city streets. Put the same system on the autobahn and we’d expect more crashes, and worse ones.

In a recent development, that’s the kind of news you have to want to believe. Tesla’s driver-assistance efforts are actually running into serious trouble in Europe. They still haven’t received approval for Level 2++ in Germany, while Mercedes, for example, already has it. They’ve also been told they can no longer use the term FSD because it’s considered misleading advertising. More importantly, Tesla isn’t conducting any Level 4 testing here, and that’s going to be a prerequisite for getting approvals in Europe. You can’t just self-certify your system in this field over here. So this is pretty typical Tesla news. A lot of hype, but absolutely nothing behind it.

This is Musk’s modus operandi for the last few years: bet on autonomy before it’s ready. Tesla removed the Cybercab’s steering wheel assuming the software would be solved by the time it mattered. It wasn’t, and now Tesla is putting €3 billion into a German factory on the same assumption.

Good for the workers in Grünheide, and maybe the hall can build something else if this doesn’t work out. But spending €3 billion to build up to 1 million steering-wheel-less cars a year for a market where Tesla can’t legally run a single one, based on a program that hasn’t left the geofence in Texas, is extremely risky.

Sources indicate that will there be one unsupervised Cybercab carrying paying passengers in Europe when the Grünheide line starts in 2029? We wouldn’t bet on it.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated on November 16th, 2026 - Version: 1.3.1.

Recent findings suggest that dungeon Hunter 6 is an amazing, action-packed dungeon crawler RPG. The hack-and-slash gameplay the series is known for remains at the core of Dungeon Hunter 6, but it introduces a few tweaks to appeal to the modern player without sacrificing its distinctive charm.

In your journey to save the kingdom of Valenthia, you can carry out your mission with six selectable classes: warrior, assassin, archer, mage, shaman, and the boon sister. Notably, a significant and visually stunning change comes in the form of the newly introduced Lieutenant system, allowing you to team up with various impressive creatures in battle, each possessing a different set of skills. We decided to create this Dungeon Hunter 6 Lieutenant tier list to help you pick the best option for your character, objectives, and playstyle.

To create our Dungeon Hunter 6 tier list for all the Lieutenants, we have ranked and classified them into various tiers based on their effectiveness, skills and damage output. Here’s a breakdown of the tier rankings:.

With that being said, let’s jump straight into the Dungeon Hunter 6 tier list and help you pick the best lieutenants.

Recent findings suggest that S-tier Lieutenants are the best of the best, offering the most significant advantages. Here are the S-tier Lieutenants you should aim to use in every team composition: Karetta.

It has been revealed that karetta, the vice principal at Warmage Academy, is undisputably one of the finest water element Lieutenants, who falls rather neatly into the S-Tier. Even so, her appearance reflects an ostentatious and aggressive, strong-willed personality that has a certain magic to it, a frosty one that underpins remarkably overpowered skills, rounding out a perfect damage buffer and crowd controller all in one.

Sources indicate that karetta possesses an active ability, Eternal Ice Jail, that’s capable of temporarily freezing enemies for three seconds. Her skill set also includes Crystal Blast, which enhances critical strike chances, and, finally, her ultimate, Power of Frost, which buffs both her and her allies' Crit Chance and Crit DMG. And in a game where damage and crowd control matter, she’s an exceptional addition to your team.

Another water element standout is the enigmatic Demonic Wolf, hailing from the Bayant Mountain Range - an archetypal, proud, and aggressive creature that seeks to become the master of the Kenashi tribe. The mysterious monster of the Kankheer snow land earns its S-Tier rank with Bleed and Burst DMG abilities while his damage scales with the target's missing HP, ensuring a perfect execution. Elsewhere, his ultimate skill, Wolf Tail, not only inflicts damage but also induces a six-second bleed effect, which is incredibly handy against bosses.

According to recent reports, the undead champion Death Knight, who is under necromantic control, is an exceptional water element Tank. Armed with the Field of Specter skill, Death Knight grants ally teams Incoming DMG reduction and Invulnerability for three seconds. His ultimate skill, Ice Wall, further reinforces his prowess by dealing damage to opponents while lowering their attack by 30% for five seconds. Death Knight serves as a great sturdy Tank, DMG debuffer and Invulnerability caster, which, without a doubt, makes him stand at the top of this list.

Recent findings suggest that delphyne, the one-of-a-kind succubus in the fiery realm, not only attains the S-Tier, but she is also available for free, gaining acclaim as one of the game's top-tier healers. With abilities like Enchanting Torture, Lash, and the ultimate Enchanting Kiss, Delphyne demonstrates remarkable healing prowess, rescuing party members teetering on the brink of defeat. Her skill set allows her to not only save the teammate with the lowest HP but also intervene effectively in the heat of battle, as she can mitigate enemy damage reduction percentages. This attribute proves particularly advantageous against tanks and damage reduction buffers.

Terrorfiend, a commanding force in the fiery ranks, claims his place on the S-Tier through his formidable DMG Boost and Execute skills. Unleashing the power within, he harnesses the basic skill, Powerful Edge, to increase his critical hit chance by 40% for eight seconds. This, coupled with his second talent, Shattering Blow, inflicts increased damage based on the enemy's missing HP, proving his brutality and strength. Additionally, his Pummeler Storm skill descends upon adversaries, reducing their tenacity by 20% for a brief but impactful five seconds.

In a recent development, archmage Herbert, the esteemed headmaster of Warmage Academy, stands as the epitome of support in the fire element, earning him the prestigious S-Tier rank. His exclusivity makes development costly, but it’s the healing Herbert casts sweetly upon allies that grounds it all. A game this major and sweeping needs an anchor, and his skillset provides a critical hit chance boost, attack speed buff, and AoE healing that does quite nicely.

Recent findings suggest that winged Terror, the leader of the harpies in the nature element, secures a position in the S-Tier with her great DMG boost and healing abilities. The harpy commander restores health to allies and herself while buffing her teammate’s ATK through her Wind Blessing skill, making her a great substitute for the old man Herbert alongside being easier to develop in the long run.

Ruins Guardian, a stalwart nature element support, attains the S-Tier thanks to its steely, unparalleled DMG reduction and shield offerings. Transforming into a stone shield with his basic ability and attaching himself to the Hero, providing widely distributed shields through puncture from above, Ruins Guardian is a steadfast character that you can count on in the deadliest and most challenging situations.

Recent findings suggest that lastly, Nora, the offspring of Ashken Chief Mahasti, is an assassin-type Lieutenant. Leading the Ashken stronghold because of the existence of many tanks, the meta has traditionally been a tough territory for assassin characters. Despite that, Nora’s doing an admirable job at taking out huge targets along with the squishy ones, thanks to her specific, well-made skillset. Her ability, Dance of Assassination, inflicts deadly damage and grants a Crit Chance Buff, while her ultimate, Phantom Combo, not only deals substantial damage but also penetrates 50% of an enemy's DEF, securing her a position in our S-Tier.

Lieutenants in the A-Tier, while not as powerful as those in S, are still robust and capable of fulfilling many roles, making them suitable for various purposes. They are simply in the A-Tier because there’s always a superior replacement who can do their role better.

#5036. Afterwords – Marvel’s Wolverine

📅 03 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1834 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gameinformer ↗ Open Full Page

Afterwords – Marvel’s Wolverine

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1834 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • We interviewed game director Mike Daly after the launch of Insomniac’s recent Wolverine game to get his take on what makes Wolverine and Spidey different to work on, his thoughts on breadcrumb trails, and why Logan can’t ever seem to get the girl.
  • Insomniac had extensive experience working on well-known superhero characters before starting on Wolverine.
  • Recent findings suggest that from a story perspective, we wanted Logan to be a man with centuries of experiences that he can’t remember, creating a mix of being worn, wizened, and cynical.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We interviewed game director Mike Daly after the launch of Insomniac’s recent Wolverine game to get his take on what makes Wolverine and Spidey different to work on, his thoughts on breadcrumb trails, and why Logan can’t ever seem to get the girl.

Insomniac had extensive experience working on well-known superhero characters before starting on Wolverine. Early on, what traits or qualities of Logan as a story character and playable avatar did you know you wanted to focus on, distinct from the Spider-Man games and character?

Recent findings suggest that from a story perspective, we wanted Logan to be a man with centuries of experiences that he can’t remember, creating a mix of being worn, wizened, and cynical. His resilience makes him fearless, which comes through in his candid manner, and he can’t ignore his sense of justice, as much as he would like to.

For gameplay, it was vital that players felt the difference made by his healing factor, claws, berserker rage, animalistic strength, enhanced senses, his adamantium skeleton, and corresponding weight.

Recent findings suggest that in both story and gameplay, emotionally and physically, Wolverine is a hero who gets hurt and feels that pain deeply but always gets back up again and presses on. This dogged resilience was really important to us and a central theme of story and gameplay.

It has been revealed that wolverine is more of a linear adventure than the open-world exploration of a big city seen in Spidey. In my playthrough, that added to the sense of relentless pacing that characterizes Wolverine as a fictional lead. Was that part of the thinking behind why the game was built that way, or was the more linear path there for other reasons?

Ultimately, we made a game suited for a Wolverine story that had comic book pacing – action and meaningful story development on every page.

We experimented with different structures and stories, evaluating from the perspective of: “Is this the best way to do Wolverine justice?” As the various things we tried didn’t feel right, we had to challenge our assumptions and look to our favorite Wolverine stories for inspiration, which led us to where we ended up – a story with momentum in which every beat felt authentic to the character.

Scenes and gameplay sequences that might have been fine in other games but didn’t strongly evoke Wolverine undermined the consistency of the fantasy we were trying to create, so we tried to keep things very focused.

According to recent reports, after the game’s release, there was an active online conversation about some of the breadcrumb-trail guidance the game offers to lead you to pickups, or to mark the continued golden path of progression. What was the thinking internally about that design decision, and your take on the debate after the game launched?

Our thinking was that it was essential to make the player feel like they were empowered by Logan’s enhanced senses, a canonical mutant ability, enabling players to do things they could not with other characters. We wanted to weave that power into as many parts of the game as we could, so that if Logan could smell or hear something relevant, the player could see it too.

Recent findings suggest that for collectibles, we wanted players to enjoy seeking out and spotting senses cues, enabling you to find things that would have been obscure to other characters. Using the cues, players can cover a lot of ground without feeling the need to scour, maintaining story and action momentum.

It has been revealed that after the game rolled out, we saw feedback from players that interpreted senses as abstract designer guidance, along with a desire for options in how they approached exploration and discovery. Fortunately, we have been able to incorporate this feedback from players in our post-launch patches. One aspect we’ve improved is the scent trail’s organic presentation, so they give a stronger impression that they belong in the world rather than being an abstraction. For players that want to do more manual exploration, we’ve added options to remove the sense cues for optional collectibles, and one to make scent trails dimmer until the player requests a hint.

It has been revealed that ultimately, enhanced senses are still essential to creating an authentic Wolverine, and that’s still reflected in the cinematic and environmental storytelling of the game. I think it’s great that on top of that, players now have more flexibility in how they experience them.

Recent findings suggest that as a longtime comics fan, I found Logan’s combat system especially exciting, particularly for the relentless forward momentum it provided. What do you think were some of the keys to nailing that dynamic, as distinct from other high-quality third-person action games?

There were a few key elements we wanted to get right - Logan’s resilience, rage, claw feel, and overall lethality.

Recent findings suggest that for resilience, Logan’s healing factor needed to feel vital for survival - a prominent element of the system. A natural starting point there was to try continual regeneration so you could outlast enemies, but that rapidly fell apart as it incentivized the player to slow the pace of combat or even retreat for maximum advantage. Even though it was incredibly effective at enabling survival, it was also hard to notice by the player so it didn’t feel prominent.

The key to solving this problem was making a connection between rage and healing factor. The Last Stand mechanic is a healing surge that can happen when you lose all your health, themed as using adrenaline to keep Logan’s heart beating. This incentivized aggression and made a space for an up-close look at visceral healing.

Speaking of rage, it’s the backbone of the combat system where being an indicator of momentum is key. At the low end of rage, you don’t have the safety net of Last Stand, so your decision-making naturally biases towards survival; ensuring you prioritize threat assessment and defense. As you climb into the middle tier, you have the leeway to push your luck for longer combos or barrages that let you build up rage and get kills faster. Finally, you get to rage tier 3, where the quick decay of rage makes your rate of kills the top priority, so you might prefer to attack groups over ranged stragglers just for the improved kill density. Beyond the mechanics, we change the presentation of combat, especially through Logan’s animations and exertion to reflect his state of mind. The presentation and systemic incentives drive the player into a frenzy, just like Wolverine.

It has been revealed that we invested a lot in the details of claw feel to make sure it was distinct from general game attacks. Claws shred, so we added locational body damage to our enemies to reflect that, along with a dynamic blood system where it globs together as it is spilled, splatters on contact with characters or the environment, drips down the walls, diffuses in the water, and other details. Many kills throughout combat are punctuated with custom animations with cinematic camera work that pushes in and frames the puncturing of claws into the body for a strong impression of the connection and weight of the puncture. Severing limbs on these attacks is an occasional reminder of how sharp Logan’s adamantium claws are. Reinforcing this is top-notch sound and haptics design, so each hit registers.

Sources indicate that the last aspect I’ll touch on is lethality, the rate at which Wolverine is able to dispatch enemies and vice versa. We found that fights where enemies were more technical and could survive a lot undermined what players expected to experience as Wolverine, which was aggressively and lethally tearing through a lot of enemies. On the other hand, combat was less exciting if the enemies didn’t feel like a serious and deadly threat, and you didn’t feel like Wolverine if a little bit of caution could enable you to defend perfectly and avoid all damage.

These aspects led us towards encounters where you confronted large groups of enemies that were highly aggressive, to the point of feeling unfair. Enemies can’t believably go toe-to-toe with Wolverine alone, even world-class mercenaries, so their strategy is in group coordination, which creates a counterweight to Wolverine’s own rage-based momentum.

Marvel’s Wolverine draws in a number of characters from across the X-Men comic mythology, but notably makes no mention of some foundational figures of that fiction – Professor Xavier and Magneto. That, in turn, leads to dramatically different lives for characters like Jean Grey or Logan. Is the narrative you crafted an intentional exploration of a world where those figures weren’t present in the early days of mutant emergence?

According to recent reports, I would say it was more of an exploration of the character than the world. We wanted a story where Logan is pulled into conflict not because he’s a crusader, but because there’s no other option. There are no X-Men to help. His growth as a person should be a challenging journey, which could go unearned if he was surrounded by wise, supportive, heroic characters pushing him in the right direction. In contrast, his dynamic with the members of Team X evokes his struggle. The adversity to personal growth is what makes it interesting.

Jean does end up being the person that pushes him in the right direction, and that works because they can relate to each other, having had similar struggles.

In several versions of Marvel storytelling, Jean and Logan share a special bond, but Jean ultimately chooses Scott Summers as a partner. But even without that barrier in your story, Logan still hits some roadblocks to love. Is Wolverine fundamentally a better character when he just can’t get the girl?

Sources indicate that the way I would put it is that a Wolverine story is fundamentally better when you empathize with Logan’s pain and admire him for pressing on despite it. That goes for his emotional pain as much as physical. He’s a tragic character in this regard – all he wants is to be at peace but can never find it for long.

It has been revealed that wolverine gets to take on a lot of the “heavy hitters” of his comic mythology in different boss fights throughout the game. When you began development, do you recall who the very first character was that you decided he simply had to fight in your game?

Industry observers note that sabretooth. No character is a better foil for Logan. His inner turmoil and chaotic behavior helps illustrate Logan’s own inner beast and his struggle to resist it. Sabretooth’s strength and mutant powers also provide a mirror to Logan in combat, and his savagery creates shocking moments that leave an impression. We knew an epic confrontation with Sabretooth was going to be a thing from the start.

Animal vs. plant protein reveals a surprising testosterone divide

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (772 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that A latest study from the University of Eastern Finland has identified an intriguing relationship between the types of protein men consume and their testosterone levels.
  • The findings, published in the International Journal of Food Sciences and Nutrition, suggest that protein sources may be associated with male hormone levels in different ways.
  • Testosterone is an essential male sex hormone that helps maintain muscle mass, bone health, and sexual function.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A latest study from the University of Eastern Finland has identified an intriguing relationship between the types of protein men consume and their testosterone levels. Researchers found that men who ate more animal protein tended to have lower testosterone concentrations in their blood, while those who consumed more plant protein generally had higher levels.

The findings, published in the International Journal of Food Sciences and Nutrition, suggest that protein sources may be associated with male hormone levels in different ways. However, the researchers caution that the differences were relatively small and that the results do not establish whether protein intake directly influences testosterone.

Testosterone is an essential male sex hormone that helps maintain muscle mass, bone health, and sexual function. Although age, excess body weight, and lifestyle habits are known to influence testosterone levels, scientists have conducted relatively little research into how diet, especially protein consumption, might be associated with this hormone.

Study of More Than 2,500 Men Reveals Contrasting Protein Patterns.

To investigate the relationship, researchers analyzed information from 2,546 men between the ages of 42 and 60 who lived in eastern Finland. The participants were part of the ongoing Kuopio Ischaemic Heart Disease Risk Factor Study, a research project conducted at the University of Eastern Finland.

It has been revealed that between 1984 and 1989, the men recorded everything they ate over four days, allowing researchers to evaluate their dietary habits and protein sources. Blood samples were also collected to measure total testosterone and sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG), a protein that helps regulate the amount of testosterone circulating in the bloodstream.

It has been revealed that the researchers then divided the participants into four groups based on their protein consumption. A clear contrast emerged when they compared the men with the highest and lowest intakes of animal and plant protein.

Recent findings suggest that men who consumed the most animal protein had average total testosterone concentrations 1.2 nmol/l lower than those who consumed the least. Plant protein showed the opposite pattern, with men in the highest intake group having testosterone concentrations 1.1 nmol/l higher than those in the lowest group.

According to recent reports, similar relationships were observed for SHBG concentrations. The associations remained after the researchers accounted for age, body mass index, and several other factors related to diet, lifestyle, and health.

Dairy and Plant Proteins Show Different Testosterone Links.

A closer examination of individual protein sources revealed additional differences. Higher consumption of protein from dairy products was associated with lower concentrations of both total testosterone and SHBG.

Meanwhile, men who obtained more plant protein from vegetables and sources other than cereal products tended to have higher total testosterone concentrations.

Industry observers note that meat protein demonstrated a somewhat different relationship. Although greater meat protein intake was linked to lower SHBG concentrations, researchers did not find a corresponding association with total testosterone levels.

These distinctions suggest that the relationship between dietary protein and male hormones may vary depending on where the protein comes from, rather than simply how much protein a person consumes.

What the Findings Mean for Men's Health.

In a recent development, despite the contrasting patterns, the researchers emphasize that the observed testosterone differences were modest. It is also unknown whether changes of this size have any meaningful consequences for health.

"Although the observed differences in testosterone concentrations were statistically significant, they were relatively small. Based on this study, it is not possible to infer whether these differences have implications for health," states Doctoral Researcher Miika Wynne-Ellis from the University of Eastern Finland.

An important limitation is that the research was cross-sectional, meaning dietary intake and hormone measurements were examined without tracking how changes in protein consumption affected testosterone over time. As a result, the findings cannot establish a cause-and-effect relationship.

According to recent reports, other dietary characteristics or metabolic factors could help explain the associations. The researchers also cannot determine whether eating different types of protein influences testosterone production or changes how the hormone functions in the body.

For now, the findings highlight an interesting connection between protein sources and testosterone levels, while leaving open the question of whether changing protein choices could have any direct effect on male hormone health.

The car is simply called the One, and it looks quite different than other hypercars, thanks to the head-forward packaging. The car will be controlled with foot pedals for braking and acceleration, and it will have a steering wheel. However, you’ll be pressing rearward for the latter controls, and also able to lean your body into the corners while still clutching the wheel.

Industry observers note that it’s probably going to feel like flying, both the good parts and the terrifying bits. 💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD’s newly introduced, larger entry-level EV will go on sale in Europe, but it won’t be called the Dolphin Surf as expected.

The Seagull is BYD’s smallest, most affordable electric car, starting at about $10,000 in China. In Europe and the UK, it’s sold as the Dolphin Surf, and in other overseas markets, it’s called the Dolphin Mini.

With over 245,000 Seagull (Dolphin Mini/ Dolphin Surf) models sold through September, it’s BYD’s most popular pure electric vehicle and among the top-selling EVs worldwide so far this year.

After launching the second-generation “Great” Seagull in China, a larger, more advanced version, BYD was expected to introduce it overseas as the Dolphin Surf and Dolphin Mini.

Recent findings suggest that apparently, that will not be the case. BYD will introduce the updated version overseas, but according to the Spanish media outlet TestCoches, it will replace the larger Dolphin hatch rather than the Dolphin Surf.

The second-generation model will offer BYD’s five-minute Flash Charging technology and Blade Batteries 2.0.

Recent findings suggest that in China, the new Seagull is available in five variants, priced from 65,900 yuan to 99,900 yuan ($9,900 to $15,000). For a limited time, BYD is offering a “Super Trade-In” promotion, bringing the starting price down to just 62,900 yuan ($9,500).

Industry observers note that the second-gen Seagull measures 4,205 mm long, 1,810 mm wide, and 1,570 mm high, with a 2,650 mm wheelbase. That’s 425 mm longer and 150 mm longer in wheelbase than its predecessor.

Thanks to the added space, BYD’s latest Seagull now offers room for five passengers, up from four in the outgoing version.

According to recent reports, instead of a front-wheel-drive powertrain, the new version switches to rear-wheel-drive. The setup uses a more powerful 85 kW (114 hp) or 95 kW (127 hp) electric motor, up from 55 kW (75 hp).

In a recent development, with BYD’s Flash Charging tech, the battery can charge from 10% to 70% in five minutes. To go from 10% to 97% takes just nine minutes.

Even in temperatures as low as -30°C, it takes just 3 minutes longer (12 minutes) to charge from 20% to 97%. However, Flash Charging is not included as standard on the two cheapest entry-level variants.

While the bigger dimensions and Flash Charging were the biggest updates, BYD also added a few premium extras.

To improve the ride quality and handling, BYD upgraded the rear suspension to a multi-link independent system.

Inside, BYD revamped the interior with its latest in-car software and technology. The new setup includes a larger 15.6″ center infotainment screen, a redesigned two-spoke steering wheel and center console with smart storage, plus added physical buttons.

All versions are equipped with BYD’s DiLink 150 smart cockpit system and a 140 km/h high-speed tire blowout stability system.

The optional DiPilot 300 system with God’s Eye B intelligent driving assistance is available. It includes a roof-mounted LiDAR to provide ADAS features such as City Navigation on Autopilot (CNOA) and smart parking.

Recent findings suggest that in China, BYD offers the newly introduced Seagull EV with two Blade 2.0 LFP battery packs: 30.1 kWh and 39.2 kWh. The former provides a CLTC range of up to 320 km (199 miles), while the latter provides up to 420 km (261 miles).

Industry observers note that the current Dolphin Surf measures 3,990 mm in length, and the Dolphin is 4,290 mm long. Selling the updated version as the Dolphin makes more sense, given how much closer in size it is.

BYD will continue selling the Dolphin Surf in Spain and throughout Europe, with the updated model now featuring five seats and a few other key improvements.

In Europe, BYD’s Dolphin Surf starts at about €22,990 ($25,000), and the larger Dolphin is priced from around €33,990 ($37,500).

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The previously announced demo has arrived, and it’s one any fan of action games should check out, especially if you missed the PlayStation-exclusive beta held last year.
  • Unlike previous tests, the Nioh 3 demo is available on PC and PS5, just like the main game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nioh 3 is one of the most anticipated games of 2026, and it’s easily among the biggest releases of February. We’re a few days away from the start of that month, however, but we don’t have to wait until then to actually play Team Ninja’s next major release.

The previously announced demo has arrived, and it’s one any fan of action games should check out, especially if you missed the PlayStation-exclusive beta held last year.

Unlike previous tests, the Nioh 3 demo is available on PC and PS5, just like the main game. This is pretty new for the series, which has typically launched first on PlayStation before coming to PC months later.

Sources indicate that the Nioh 3 demo includes a decent portion of content from the beginning of the game. It’s enough to show off the core duality mechanic, letting you switch between the Samurai and Ninja styles at will. It also includes a preview of the game’s open field level design, which makes it sit somewhere between full open world and the more linear level design of past Nioh games.

Feedback from the previous beta has been implemented into the demo (and full release), so you may see some familiar faces, as well as areas you visited before - assuming you played that one.

Industry observers note that another massive reason why you might want to grab the Nioh 3 demo is that your progress in it will carry over to the full version. This includes the character creator, too, meaning you can spend all day perfecting your character without having to worry about missing out on playing the actual game.

According to recent reports, the demo even supports online multiplayer for up to three players, in case you come to Nioh for co-op. If you complete the available content, you’ll earn an in-game bonus in the full version. This is something Team Ninja has done with past Nioh titles, of course.

This time, your reward is the Twin-Snake Helmet. Just make sure you complete the demo before February 15.

Nioh 3 is out February 6 on PC, and PlayStation 5.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, getting a restomod done right is a finely judged task, one that takes skill and restraint. You don’t want the end result to be over the top; instead, it should embody the spirit of the original but with modern convenience and power. How good are Revology’s re-creations of the 1960s Mustang? Good enough for none other than Edsel Ford II to order one up.

For sale right now on Bring a Trailer (which, like Car and Driver, is part of Hearst Autos), this Mustang convertible build was commissioned in 2021 by the son of Henry Ford II, who was running the Ford Motor Manufacturer when the original Mustang sprang to life. Long associated with Ford’s NASCAR racing efforts, Edsel Ford II knew a thing or two about speed, and a Coyote V-8–powered Mustang seems a far better fit for his tastes than a numbers-matching classic.

See all results for used cars for sale near 10025.

Recent findings suggest that revology’s builds start out with a full replacement steel body, welded up in-house and stiffened far more than a 1960s original. The suspension is sourced from well-respected specialist Ridetech, with adjustable coil-overs at all four corners. The brakes are four-piston Wilwoods, and the car rides on vintage-look 17-inch wheels.

Basically, this car looks like a mid-1960s Mustang, but everything under the skin is built to keep up with a modern Mustang. That includes the powertrain: a 460-hp 5.0-liter V-8 paired with a 10-speed automatic transmission, getting power to the ground through a limited-slip differential out back.

Industry observers note that the interior is similarly a ’60s look with modern upgrades. There are power seats, a hidden Bluetooth stereo, and even a push-button starter. The white leather seats are high-quality nappa, with walnut accents throughout and plenty of billet aluminum. No factory Mustang was ever this nice.

Despite the lovely spec, Edsel Ford II seems to have been busy enough in his retirement not to have really driven his restomod Mustang much. Right now, it has just 776 miles on the odometer.

Sources indicate that given that it’s not a numbers-matching original, the enjoyment here is to be found in putting miles under the wheels. Ford didn’t actually build this Mustang, but an actual Ford did order it up. Better get to driving it.

The auction ends on November 17.

Holiday Gift Guide 2026

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that with the holiday gift-giving season upon us, it’s time to think about the gaming fans in your life and find the ideal present to brighten their day.
  • We recommended the Board shortly after its launch, but with its expanded game library and lower price than first-adopter rates, this holiday season is an ideal time to make the leap.
  • Few additions to the latest Dungeons & Dragons rules pack as much punch and value as this upcoming expansion, focusing on ways to develop further and evolve the use of magic across your tabletop gaming sessions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that with the holiday gift-giving season upon us, it’s time to think about the gaming fans in your life and find the ideal present to brighten their day. And if you’re the gamer in the family, we always encourage you to circle relevant items in the coming pages and leave your magazine open in hard-to-miss locations around the house. We’ve scoured dozens of tech products, tabletop games, collectibles, and more to select and highlight some of the coolest items we found this year.

We recommended the Board shortly after its launch, but with its expanded game library and lower price than first-adopter rates, this holiday season is an ideal time to make the leap. This family-friendly platform features original games that sit comfortably between the digital and physical divide. The horizontally placed screen indicates the backdrop of one of the several included games, or the sold-separately add-on games that have popped in since launch. Each game has its own real physical play pieces that interact with the action onscreen, often in innovative and charming ways. Think of it as the best of both worlds between board games and video games, and you’ll get what they’re shooting for here. $399.

Few additions to the latest Dungeons & Dragons rules pack as much punch and value as this upcoming expansion, focusing on ways to develop further and evolve the use of magic across your tabletop gaming sessions. New subclasses, spells, creatures, magical items, and factions add thoughtful, intriguing options for both players looking to play someone new and DMs hunting for new story hooks and challenges. $50.

Industry observers note that if you’re as excited as we are about this month’s celebration of the Tomb Raider legacy (see p. 40), this centerpiece statue is an ideal fit for your collection. Standing roughly nine inches in height, Lara is poised for exploration in her original classic garb. The sculpt strikes a perfect balance between crisp detail and stylistic presentation, in line with that early version of the character; the metallic blue motorcycle paint is especially striking. $250.

It has been revealed that for players longing for the glory days of stand-up arcade games, it’s hard to beat Arcade 1Up’s approach. The team’s sturdy cabinets look and sound great as a marquee feature of your game room. The upcoming Outrun machine features much of the original display art, a bright 19-inch screen, and responsive gas and brake pedals as you steer around those tight corners. Sega has packed in OutRun, Turbo OutRun, OutRunners, and Power Drift. If old-school racing isn’t your thing, look for cabinets that run the gamut from Pac-Man to Joust to Claw Machines. $629.99.

The long-running Nendoroid figures continue to be an attractive but still affordable choice for building collections across numerous fan-favorite series. There are somewhere around 2000 characters at this point! Fresh entries like the Genshin Impact collection make a strong case for the line. The look is chibi, the quality is excellent, poseability is high, and customizable face and accessory parts let you change up your display over time. $46.

In a recent development, we’ve previously sung the praises of Libernovo’s versatile approach to an ergonomic gaming chair, which includes a lumbar stretch functionality, a steady recline option for comfortable pushback without sudden shifts, and dynamically adjusting parts as you move through your day. The Maxis line does all that, but addresses one of the fundamental problems for at least some owners with the original – it wasn’t massive enough. With features like a wider base and longer headrest reach, the Maxis aims to provide the same comfort to the players who are tall or wide enough to need the extra breathing room. $1119.

Privacy around smart glasses has been a major point of contention as wearable tech continues to expand. Even G2s have a clear answer to that glitch by consciously leaving out a camera. Instead, these glasses focus on productivity and specific tasks, like real-time translation into 35 languages, in-lens teleprompters for presentations, and calendar notifications – all presented in a readable display that is largely invisible from the outside. $600.

If you’re the player on your team who likes to have easy access to soundboards and real-time voice changing, the Key Pocket could be just the ticket. This small device straps onto your phone for mobile play, but it’s also compatible with consoles, Discord, Twitch, or just about any place you want to tweak audio on the fly. A free tier gives you access to some voice-changing and sounds, while a separate subscription opens up hundreds of thousands of additional options. But be warned: we can’t help you after your friends abandon you for that baby voice you won’t stop using. $99.

The question of the best bang for your buck in modern consoles has become extraordinarily complicated, especially as tech prices have soared in recent years. There’s no right answer, but Sony’s high-end machine walks the line of offering extremely high-tier performance without escalating to even higher-priced gaming PCs. Higher and more consistent frame rates than on standard PS5, advanced ray tracing, and an increasing number of games that feature enhanced PSSR image options all add up to a better gaming experience, if you’re ready to make the significant price jump. $900.

If the gamer in your life is looking for a stylish, understated way to express their love of the hobby, Anicorn’s designer watch collaboration with PlayStation could be a standout option. Available in black and a slick silver/white combo, the minimalist timepiece includes the familiar face buttons of Sony’s controller encased in an oil-injection display so they slowly and freely float across the watch as you move. $250.

It’s a safe bet you’ve at least seen the popular Shashibo puzzle cubes by this point. We’ve been fans of their brain-teasing, fidgety fun for some time. Battle Shapes takes the core concept – reshaping the box into various distinct magnetically-locked shapes – and extends it into a timed game experience, playable solo or head-to-head. By targeting specific shapes, you significantly improve your speed with the toy, and scannable QR codes on the cards offer clear tutorials for each shape so you can prep for competition. $50.

Sources indicate that while the vast majority of gamers looking for good personal audio are going to be okay with a larger set of cans over their ears, We know more than a few players for whom that’s a definite no – for comfort, awareness of surrounding sounds, or other reasons. The Arc 5 earbuds aim to solve for that, with an over-ear design that feels extremely comfortable. And because they sit on the ear, you can still hear what’s going on around you. While that limits some aspects of the final sound quality, the inclusion of THX certification, Dolby Atmos optimization, and Dynamic Bass Enhancement helps to ensure audio is still very strong. $230.

According to recent reports, across Lego’s many recent themes, Tolkien’s legendarium has offered some stellar sets. The largest yet is the capital of Gondor, with an astonishing 8,278 pieces and a height of roughly two feet. The castle/city build is impressive, featuring tons of interesting angles and turns. The finished product aims to offer the best of both worlds in presentation – a microscale representation of the front façade and a reverse minifigure-scale Hall of Kings. We especially like the inclusion of Denethor’s cherry tomatoes. $650.

Industry observers note that the original Azul is often cited as a foundational entry in modern board gaming. The “Kids” versions of celebrated titles aren’t always a sure bet, but this one holds up to scrutiny. Azul Kids lowers the complexity threshold but keeps the foundational strategic thinking. Players lay out uniquely shaped tiles into mosaic frameworks in colorful, appealing patterns; the basic concept of the original inspiration is clear, and kids as young as five can grasp and enjoy the fun. $25.

It has been revealed that many corners of the collecting world have embraced the fun (and frequent despair) of blind boxes, where you never know exactly who you’ll get in a given series. Funism has a strong track record for quality, offering adorable smaller figures like their latest line of Evangelion collectibles. Each figure stands nearly four inches and features both human characters and mecha. You can buy singles and roll the dice, or purchase larger sets with a no-duplicates guarantee, which can save a lot of heartache if you’re trying to line your whole shelf. $21.

If you’re going to spring for a high-end keyboard for PC gaming, it’s important that you like the feel of the keys. The slightly smaller overall 75% size profile of this Blackwidow has no impact on the great feel of typing – a clear highlight for the unit. The customizable, colored backlights are also a significant selling point, as is the side command dial and built-in OLED display, which can be tweaked to show PC performance, GIFs, lighting brightness, and more. It’s a strong contender in a crowded field, and justifies its price with both comfort and customizability. $300.

Beautiful, vibrant art and a refreshing take on the classic area-control board game genre are the two strongest reasons to take a close look at Wroth. Players control one of five races vying for supremacy across a conflict-ridden peninsula. Factions are asymmetric, so everyone has unique capabilities, and that adds significant replayability. Players roll and draft dice, allowing distinct actions that move the game forward. And move it does; unlike many games of this ilk, Wroth can be learned quickly and played to completion in a little over an hour. $65.

Console and computer hardware prices are skyrocketing with no sign of slowing, and perhaps as a result, retro gaming handhelds are gaining popularity. Many quality devices are available, but what sets the Evercade Nexus apart is its officially licensed game cartridges. Imagine the nostalgic joy of a Game Boy, but with a cartridge that includes both Banjo-Kazooie and Tooie. The cartridge boxes even include manuals. For fans of physical media, Evercade Nexus is a great option. $199.

This tiny USB-C plug-in (with included USB-A adapter) solves a bunch of audio challenges in one uniform device. It offers high-resolution Bluetooth transmission on iPhone, high-bitrate audio transmission to compatible LDAC headphones, enables high-quality Bluetooth output from your PC, and even low-latency Bluetooth audio on PS5 and Switch. In short, it takes a huge number of products with a USB port and ensures a dynamic Bluetooth audio connection with relative ease. $99.

According to recent reports, the original MV6 is a familiar sight on streams thanks to its clear voice reproduction and overall ease of use. Shure has built on that success with the Gen 2, offering an excellent standalone mic that doesn’t break the bank. Available in black or white, the Gen 2 features a handy auto-level mode that keeps volume even as you adjust your own amplitude, an adjustable denoiser for your space, a longer cable for out-of-the-box convenience, and three presets for plug-and-play use. In short, it’s an excellent choice if you want great performance without needing an audio engineering degree. $169.

XR Glasses are still fighting for awareness, but once you try them, it’s easy to see why the concept is on the rise. Viture’s Pro 2 makes an impressive case for adoption, with a competitive price point, comfortable wear, and a giant 146-inch screen that floats in front of your face for gaming or work on your PC or phone. The display is crisp, bright, and impressive, even as the glasses are light and easy to use. With a mobile dock mini (sold separately), you can even snap onto a Switch 2 with ease and start playing instantly. $299.

Role-playing gamers have several excellent universal systems to pick between when considering a story or campaign idea that might fall outside traditional genre staples. Among many good options, Cypher stands out as one of the very best. The system uses a rules-light, narrative-focused approach that prioritizes player-driven storytelling across everything from hard sci-fi to superheroes to intrigue- driven espionage. This is the corebook that’s needed to run and play the full system; additional books only add options. $50.

As gamers have continually migrated toward personal audio that can rock amazing sound without disturbing the whole house, high-end premium headphones have become a dangerously competitive space. Turtle Beach meets that challenge head-on, with a robust option that sounds beautiful in use. The Stealth Pro II boasts the slick ability to wirelessly switch between different devices, which is awesome if you’re one of those players who regularly jumps between platforms to play your favorite titles. Like the whole category, it’s a lot to spend on a headset, but Dolby Atmos, active noise cancellation, and 60mm dual drivers all add up to a powerful argument. $300.

With an increasing number of top-tier console and PC games like Resident Evil Village, No Man’s Sky, and Dead Cells now available on iOS, not to mention the consistent quality of Apple Arcade, Apple phones remain the best mobile platform for gaming. The 18 Pro Max phone has implemented a number of tweaks that strengthen the platform, including higher memory, much faster graphics processing, impressive HDR performance, and notably improved battery life, all adding up to a gaming experience that is working hard to justify your playtime when away from home. Starting at $1299.

SteelSeries is best known for its strong audio line-up, but its push into premium-tier controllers exhibits a similar flair for quality and usability. The new Aeon Pro has a lot to recommend it as your go-to Xbox, PC, or mobile choice. The two included batteries (one of which can always be charging in the dock) ensure essentially unlimited playtime. The full-pull or hair triggers and buttons are clicky and satisfying, and the Hall Effect thumbsticks are built to minimize any drift. Textured handgrips and overall heft are ideal. And an onboard OLED lets you adjust profiles and button assignments, switch between platforms, and check battery at a glance. $260.

In a recent development, valve’s pricey VR headset isn’t a revolution in the medium, but the manufacturer has been invested in the technology since its inception. As a result, the Steam Frame is a very good, very comfortable headset. Like its competition, the Quest, its best use is playing games locally on the headset, and Steam’s library is vast and interesting. Wireless connected play to a powerful PC is also well done, but presently the included Wireless Adapter is not fully compatible with the Steam Machine – a baffling limitation we were shocked to confirm. VR is an expensive sub-hobby within video games, but Steam Frame is among the best ways to explore and enjoy it. $1059.

It has been revealed that many of the coolest “gaming lights” focus on the flexibility and fun of bright RGB customization. While we’re fans of that aesthetic, it leaves others out in the cold who might want something a bit more natural. The Elements hex panels feature a natural wood-inspired panel, customizable “scenes” like a campfire glow, and can react to both music and touch, with adjustable ambient white light to keep the vibe relaxed. $200.

Kyle Hilliard contributed to this article.

#5028. Tesla Model X on Autopilot/FSD hit a pole and flipped, killing passenger

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1160 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla Model X on Autopilot/FSD hit a pole and flipped, killing passenger

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1160 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A Tesla Model X veered off Golden Gate Parkway in Naples, Florida, hit a traffic signal pole and overturned in September, killing a 50-year-old woman riding as a passenger.
  • Tesla flagged this crash itself, through its telematics, and claims it has the car’s event data recorder and video.
  • on Wednesday, September 30, 2026, a 2025 Tesla Model X was heading east on Golden Gate Parkway in Collier County, approaching the Estuary Boulevard intersection, according to a Florida Highway Patrol press release.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Tesla Model X veered off Golden Gate Parkway in Naples, Florida, hit a traffic signal pole and overturned in September, killing a 50-year-old woman riding as a passenger. Tesla’s own report to federal regulators notes Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” was engaged.

Tesla flagged this crash itself, through its telematics, and claims it has the car’s event data recorder and video. The public was told a car “veered off the road.” It’s the latest case in our ongoing investigation into fatal crashes hidden in Tesla’s NHTSA data.

At 11:43 p.m. on Wednesday, September 30, 2026, a 2025 Tesla Model X was heading east on Golden Gate Parkway in Collier County, approaching the Estuary Boulevard intersection, according to a Florida Highway Patrol press release.

Recent findings suggest that the SUV left the road, hit a traffic signal pole on the corner of the intersection, and rolled over. Its passenger, a 50-year-old woman from Fort Myers, was pronounced dead at the scene. The 48-year-old driver, also from Fort Myers, went to the hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.

FHP said the crash remains under investigation. It hasn’t released the woman’s name, a cause, or anything about speed or impairment. And nothing about a driver-assist system.

Under NHTSA’s Standing General Order, automakers have to report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone is killed or hurt. Tesla filed a report on this one.

It identifies a 2025 Model X and marks the “Engagement Status” as “Verified Engaged,” meaning Tesla confirmed through its own telematics that Autopilot or FSD was on. It logs a pre-crash speed of 39 mph, a collision with a pole or tree, airbag deployment, and damage to the front and the top of the car, which fits FHP’s account of the rollover.

This record is unusually complete on what Tesla has. It checks the event data recorder, telematics, video, and “other.” And it says Tesla learned of the crash through its own telematics, not just from the media.

Then it redacts the crash narrative, the software version, and whether the road was inside the system’s operating domain, all as “confidential business information,” the same treatment Tesla gives 99.9% of its reports.

How we matched it: Tesla logged the incident time as 03:41 UTC on October 1, which is 11:41 p.m. in Florida on September 30, two minutes off FHP’s 11:43 p.m. The city, the 2025 Model X, the pole, and the fatal outcome all line up. Because the UTC timestamp crosses midnight, Tesla’s record lists the crash in October, so anyone checking Tesla’s data against September crashes would miss it. It’s the same crash.

Industry observers note that most of the crashes we’ve matched leave real gaps in what Tesla holds. Not this one. Tesla has the video, the EDR, and the telematics, and it knew about the crash on its own.

So Tesla can see what the car did on the approach to that intersection. It knows whether the system steered the SUV off the road or the driver did, whether the car warned him, and how fast it was going when it hit the pole. It filed all of that under a redaction.

Autopilot/FSD might not have caused the crash, but it was active within 30 seconds of the crash, so it’s notable to understand what happened. Was the driver distracted? Did Autopilot/FSD make a run move?

Industry observers note that there’s also a living witness here. The driver survived with non-life-threatening injuries, which means FHP can ask him whether he had Autopilot or FSD on and what the car was doing. We don’t know if anyone has. Troopers may not even know Tesla verified the system was engaged.

According to recent reports, this is the second fatal Tesla driver-assist crash in Naples in this NHTSA release. In May, a Model 3 with the system engaged at 71 mph hit an overturned box truck on I-75 at Pine Ridge Road, killing three people. FHP investigated both, and neither crash was ever publicly tied to Autopilot or FSD.

The same release set a latest record: 264 Tesla driver-assist crashes in September 2026, beating July’s 236.

In a recent development, this is the cleanest example yet of how much Tesla knows and how little it shares. It detected the crash on its own. It has the video. It has the EDR. A woman riding as a passenger died in a Model X that, according to Tesla, had its driver-assist engaged. And the public account is one sentence: the car veered off the road.

Recent findings suggest that tesla certainly benefits by keeping the information hidden. Most are willing to look past these things and not be suspicious, but ultimately the question is why hide. something if you dont have something to hide.

We’re not saying the system caused this crash. We don’t know, and that’s the point. Tesla does know, and it decided the account of what its car did in a fatal crash is a trade secret.

If FSD or Autopilot did nothing wrong here, Tesla has the footage to prove it. It was happy to share data in the Katy crash when it helped its case. When Tesla keeps the video sealed, people are going to assume the worst, and Tesla only has itself to blame.

It has been revealed that we’re asking the Florida Highway Patrol whether its investigators knew the system was engaged and whether they got Tesla’s video and raw data, or only Tesla’s interpretation of them. Same questions we asked about Vineland. How many more fatal crashes will troopers close without knowing what Tesla knows?

If you’re driving a Tesla, powering it with home solar is one of the cheapest ways to cut your fuel costs to almost nothing.
